articles.title: New Cocktail Bar Coming to Raleigh’s North Hills Innovation District
articles.titleKo: New Cocktail Bar Coming to Raleigh’s North Hills Innovation District
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Patrick Shanahan — the hospitality visionary who has brought cinematic design to Raleigh’s most talked-about bars and restaurants this year — is bringing his signature creative sensibility to North Hills for the first time with co-owner Robby Opperman. Slated to open in 2027, Little Saint Cocktail Co. will mark Shanahan’s fifth project in two years, and North Hills’ first true standalone cocktail bar. Follow along at @LittleSaintRaleigh. Shanahan’s track record speaks for itself. Peregrine earned a James Beard Foundation nomination for “Best New Restaurant”; Capulet Cocktail Club at The Exchange was spotlighted in F orbes and Wine Enthusiast for its maximalist design; and Rosebud Cocktail Lounge in downtown Raleigh landed the cover of Raleigh Magazine’s Best Bars issue. This month, the all-day Café Royale will open at The Exchange, introducing a coffee-to-cocktail French café culture. With Little Saint, he’s bringing that same design-forward, hands-on approach to a part of the city that’s never had a dedicated craft cocktail destination of its own. “North Hills Innovation District (NHID) is a special place with a strong community of locals who come here to work, live, dine and spend time together,” said Mary Ehrenberger, Retail Leasing and Multi-Site Manager for Kane Realty Corporation. “Little Saint is a great addition to the lineup we’re building in NHID. Bringing a true cocktail bar to North Hills gives our guests another reason to linger and enjoy the neighborhood, and Patrick and his team have the creativity and hospitality experience to make this space a natural fit for the district.” Little Saint will occupy 3,865 square feet on the ground floor of the St. Albans Lofts building at 600 St Albans Drive, on the corner of St. Albans Street and Hardimont (directly across from Standard). The space will include outdoor seating along the street, adding to North Hills’ growing patio scene. As both designer and co-owner, Shanahan continues his hands-on approach to hospitality design. Little Saint will be completed by Mauer Architecture and JCI Builders, the same team behind his prior four projects. Little Saint Cocktail Co. will offer an elevated, upscale cocktail experience, filling a longstanding gap in North Hills for a dedicated craft cocktail destination. Follow along at @littlesaintraleigh for updates as the 2027 opening approaches. But first: Café Royale opens late September 2026 at The Exchange in Raleigh’s Midtown. Follow @CafeRoyaleRaleigh for opening updates. The post New Cocktail Bar Coming to Raleigh’s North Hills Innovation District appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Chicken Salad Chick, the nation’s only fast casual chicken salad restaurant concept, announced today the opening of its first restaurant in New York, which will expand the brand’s footprint to 27 states. The local community is invited to celebrate this grand opening on Tuesday, September 22, when the first 100 guests in line will win free chicken salad for a year*. The new restaurant is located in The Shops at Village Plazaat 5 Southside Drive in Clifton Park. Chicken Salad Chick is known for its dozen-plus variety of made-from-scratch chicken salad flavors, fresh sides, gourmet soups, signature sandwiches, and desserts. The new Clifton Park restaurant offers in-restaurant dining, take-out, third-party delivery, and catering options. During the grand opening week, guests can expect to experience the Southern hospitality Chicken Salad Chick is known for while taking advantage of various specials and giveaways. These include: Tuesday, September 22 – Free Chicken Salad for a Year to the First 100 Guests – The first guest in line at 10am will receive one FREE large Quick Chick of chicken salad per week for an entire year. The next 99 guests in line will receive one FREE large Quick Chick of chicken salad per month for a year. Wednesday, September 23 – The first 50 guests to spend a minimum of $15 will receive a free 40oz Chick Tumbler!** Thursday, September 24 – The first 50 guests to purchase two large Quick Chicks will receive a FREE large Chick Cooler!*** Friday, September 25 – The first 50 guests to spend a minimum of $15 will receive a FREE large Chicken Salad Chick Navy Tote Bag!** Saturday, September 26 – The first 50 guests to spend a minimum of $15 will receive a FREE large Quick Chick on their next visit!** Chicken Salad Chick of Clifton Park is the first restaurant to open under a 25-unit franchise agreement bringing locations to the Albany, Buffalo, Rochester, Syracuse, and the Upper Hudson Valley areas across New York. The agreement represents Chicken Salad Chick’s largest franchise development deal to date and is being spearheaded by an experienced, multi-unit fast casual restaurant group already operating several national restaurant brands in the Upstate New York market. “Entering New York is a major milestone for Chicken Salad Chick. It represents tremendous growth potential for our brand, and we’re already seeing strong demand,” said Scott Deviney, CEO and President of Chicken Salad Chick. “This opening expands our footprint to 27 states and marks our fifth new state entry this year, following openings in Utah, Minnesota, Pennsylvania and West Virginia. We’ve partnered with a franchise group that’s exceptionally seasoned in national restaurant operations, and their long-term commitment to this market makes them ideal partners as we bring Chicken Salad Chick to guests across the state. We’re excited to work alongside them and welcome our New York guests soon.” Giving back to the community is an important focus for the Clifton Park team and the Chicken Salad Chick brand, which established the CSC Foundation to support CURE Childhood Cancer and local food banks with fundraisers throughout the year. As part of pre-opening Friends & Family events in Clifton Park, the restaurant will be raising money for CAPTAIN Youth and Family Services, also known as CAPTAIN Community Human Services, which is a non-profit organization supporting individuals, families, and seniors in Saratoga County and the surrounding Capital Region. Chicken Salad Chick of Clifton Park will be open Monday – Sunday from 10am – 9pm. For more information on giveaways and specials, visit the Clifton Park restaurant’s Facebook. articles.title: Vicious Biscuit Signs Lease in Greenville, North Carolina
articles.titleKo: Vicious Biscuit Signs Lease in Greenville, North Carolina
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Vicious Biscuit, the original home of unapologetically bold biscuits, is adding an experienced multi-brand restaurant group to its growing franchise system. Operating as Gravy Crew, LLC, Chris Carnes, Ben Fields and operating partner Jonah Greenup, whose portfolio includes 11 Zaxby’s and six Chicken Salad Chick restaurants, have signed a lease for their first Vicious Biscuit in Greenville, North Carolina. The 3,000-square-foot restaurant will be located at 3030 S. Evans St. in University Commons and is expected to open late 2026. It will be Vicious Biscuit’s first franchise location in North Carolina, joining corporate-owned restaurants in Boone, Charlotte and Wilmington. The partnership brings together three operators who have worked alongside one another for nearly two decades. Carnes entered the restaurant business with Zaxby’s in 2001. Fields, who previously worked on the corporate side of Zaxby’s, joined Carnes in 2008. Greenup began with the group that same year, working his way from team member through management and eventually becoming a partner when the group added Chicken Salad Chick to its portfolio. While Carnes wasn’t looking to add another restaurant concept, Vicious Biscuit had been on his radar for some time. He first learned about Vicious Biscuit after seeing it featured on national television. Years later, while traveling to visit his son at Appalachian State University, he repeatedly passed Vicious Biscuit in Boone and noticed the crowds waiting outside. When he finally visited, what he found was different from the biscuit restaurant he expected. “I had probably passed it a dozen times and there were always people standing outside,” said Carnes. “We finally caught it without a line, went in and ordered a little bit of everything. I was expecting more of a mom-and-pop biscuit place, but as soon as I walked in, I realized this was a real concept. The food, the atmosphere and the personality of the brand were fun and edgy.” That experience prompted Carnes to take a closer look at Vicious Biscuit as a potential addition to the group’s restaurant portfolio. Carnes saw parallels to his early experience with Zaxby’s while the concept was still relatively young. “When I got into Zaxby’s more than 20 years ago, it was still early, and I saw what that could become,” Carnes said. “I told myself years ago that if I ever came across another opportunity I really believed in, I wasn’t going to let it pass me by. I like where Vicious Biscuit is today and the opportunity to grow with it.” Beyond the food and concept, Vicious Biscuit’s leadership team was an important factor in the group’s decision. After spending time with co-founder and CEO George McLaughlin and the team, Carnes saw an emerging concept with the infrastructure and experience his group wanted from a franchisor. “For an emerging brand, it feels very established,” Carnes said. “They’ve already built the infrastructure and support you’d expect from a much larger franchise system, and there are experienced people behind it. You have to love the product first, but just as important is knowing you can pick up the phone and call the people leading the company. When I met George and the team, it felt like a group of people we could work and grow with.” The group was also drawn to Vicious Biscuit’s operating model. Its single-shift schedule and 2:30 p.m. closing time offer a different operating environment from traditional full-day restaurant concepts, giving teams their afternoons and evenings back. The three partners initially signed for one restaurant, giving them an opportunity to operate within the Vicious Biscuit system before determining their next phase of growth. If Greenville performs as expected and the partnership proves to be the right long-term fit, the group sees potential for additional Vicious Biscuit restaurants in Eastern North C

articles.titleKo: Lola Beans Signs 5-Unit Deal to Enter Miami Market
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Lola Beans, the fast-growing dual drive-thru beverage concept known for handcrafted coffee, energy drinks, teas, lemonades and its signature Lola Colas (infused sodas), has signed a five-unit development agreement to enter the Miami market. The deal marks another major step in the brand’s expansion, coming just one week after Lola Beans announced a six-unit development agreement for Delaware. The new franchisees, Daniela Gonzalez and Joangel “Joey” Lopez are immigrants from Nicaragua and Cuba who grew up in Miami, where coffee was always about much more than the drink itself. They grew up surrounded by the city’s cafecito and ventanita traditions, where strong, sweet Cuban-style espresso and walk-up coffee windows have long brought people together for a quick coffee, a familiar face and conversation with a neighbor. As they started families and built their careers, Gonzalez and Lopez came to appreciate the need for a coffee experience that could keep pace with modern life without losing that sense of community. “Miami has such a strong coffee culture, but it’s also a city that moves fast,” said Gonzalez and Lopez. “We fell in love with Lola Beans because it feels close to home. It brings the spirit of Miami’s ventanita cafecito culture into a modern dual drive-thru that delivers speed without sacrificing connection. The menu goes far beyond coffee, while still keeping that personal interaction. We’re confident that combination will resonate really well here.” The couple plans to initially develop five Lola Beans locations over the next five years. “We’ve been excited for a long time about building a strong presence for Lola Beans throughout Florida, and this agreement is an important first step in that vision,” said Donny Bradley, founder of Lola Beans. “Joey and Daniela understand the culture, the community and the experience we want Lola Beans to create, and we believe they will be the first of many outstanding franchisees to help establish the brand across Florida.” The Miami agreement adds to significant momentum for Lola Beans since beginning franchising in early 2025. Last week the brand signed a six-unit development agreement for Delaware and a 120-unit Texas agreement led by Kirk and Coleen Jeter through Rise Hospitality Group, Inc. Lola Beans’ founders have hand-picked a team of industry veterans with deep experience in franchise development and operations, marketing, site selection, supply chain and procurement-all focused on giving franchisees the support they need to grow successfully nationwide. “Collectively, our team has never seen this level of interest in a brand or segment before. Our Discovery Days are filling up fast,” said John Moates, Lola Beans’ Development Partner and CDO. The post Lola Beans Signs 5-Unit Deal to Enter Miami Market appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Whit’s Frozen Custard Chooses Square as its Unified Commerce Platform
articles.titleKo: Whit’s Frozen Custard Chooses Square as its Unified Commerce Platform
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Square today announced that Whit’s Frozen Custard, the quick-service restaurant (QSR) brand known for its fresh-made frozen custard and loyal fan base, has selected Square as its unified commerce platform powering 100 locations nationwide. The move marks a pivotal step for the fast-growing franchise as it streamlines cross-location visibility, centralizes reporting and menu management, and builds a stronger foundation for continued expansion. Founded in 2003 in Granville, Ohio during one of the region’s coldest winters, Whit’s Frozen Custard began as a bold bet: that customers would fall in love with a product many had never even heard of. More than two decades later, that bet has proven sweet. With 100 locations across 11 states and a fiercely loyal following (including more than 60% repeat customers), Whit’s Frozen Custard has grown into a nationally recognized franchise known for its premium ingredients, daily fresh batches, and ever-changing “flavor of the week.” Now, under the leadership of CEO Bill Aseere – formerly a top-performing Whit’s Frozen Custard franchisee – the company is investing in the commerce platform needed to support its next chapter. “We’ve always believed that if you focus on delivering consistent quality, growth will follow,” said Aseere. “Our products and experiences upheld that standard, but as we scaled, it became clear that our technology needed to evolve alongside us. Too much time was being spent stitching gaps together across locations. We wanted to make life easier for our franchisees – enabling them to operate independently while giving our corporate team better visibility, and ultimately creating a smoother experience for our customers. Square helped us win on all fronts.” Keeping the Focus on the Custard Prior to choosing Square, Whit’s Frozen Custard operated on a combination of fragmented systems that added friction at every level of the business. Menu updates had to be manually managed across stores. Reporting lacked consistency and clarity. Franchisees were left navigating the complexities of payments, disputes, and compliance on their own. And corporate teams had limited visibility into performance and royalty tracking. Square’s franchise capabilities solved these problems in a single destination, giving the corporate team centralized control of its entities. The brand now uses Square Register, Square Kitchen Display System (KDS), Square for Restaurants, and Square for Franchises to power its growing network, removing a significant operational burden from franchisees and returning their attention to the custard that keeps customers coming back for more. In the process, franchisees see an estimated savings of approximately $2,000 annually per location across software and processing costs. “Food & beverage franchises require a delicate balance of independence on the ground and uniformity at the brand level,” said James Schonziet, Head of Food & Beverage at Square. “Square brings the operational infrastructure, reporting, and ease of use needed to scale a consistent experience across every location, while keeping it simple for the people running it day-to-day. Whit’s is a prime example of what we aim to enable on both fronts.” Serving Up the Future of QSR Through the partnership, Whit’s Frozen Custard is leaning into new ways of serving customers, including adopting Square’s emerging drive-thru capabilities to bring added speed and convenience to its operations while maintaining the brand’s signature, happy hospitality. By leveraging Square’s partner ecosystem, Whit’s is also preparing to utilize integrations that enhance online ordering, loyalty, and mobile app experiences, further enhancing how customers engage with the brand both in-store and digitally. Potbelly in West McKinney is owned and operated by father-son duo Barry and Remington Burke of Burke Restaurant Group, who bring decades of combined experience in multi-unit restaurant operations, franchising and entrepreneurship. The Burkes have long seen strong potential for Potbelly in West McKinney, drawn to the area’s growth and neighborhood-driven character. Looking ahead, the Burkes also plan to bring Potbelly to additional neighborhoods across North and East Texas as part of their 15-shop development agreement, furthering their investment in the region. “West McKinney has such a strong sense of community and a lot of energy around its growth, making it a natural fit for Potbelly,” said Remington Burke. “We’re looking forward to opening our doors and bringing residents and the local workforce together over great food and good vibes. Our team is ready to welcome longtime Potbelly fans and first-time guests alike with the craveable food, friendly service and neighborhood-driven atmosphere that define Potbelly.” To celebrate the opening, Potbelly will host a celebration on September 19 from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. Guests can enjoy a morning of food, fun and prizes with a Spin the Wheel activity featuring opportunities to win Potbelly merchandise and other giveaways, including up to 50 Free Potbelly for a Year prizes. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The portfolio encompasses 225 restaurants that collectively produce more than $1 billion in annual revenue and over $150 million in EBITDA. Authentic Restaurant Brands has secured a $325 million capital package to accelerate restaurant development and pursue additional acquisitions. The infusion came from London-based firm Trimontium. The investment includes debt and equity, with funding available as ARB identifies growth opportunities. It will support expansion across ARB’s existing markets and the selective acquisition of more regional restaurant concepts. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, ARB owns Pollo Tropical, Tavern in the Square, P.J. Whelihan’s, Mambo Seafood, and Primanti Bros. The portfolio encompasses 225 restaurants that collectively produce more than $1 billion in annual revenue and over $150 million in EBITDA. ARB has also recorded four consecutive years of positive same-store sales growth. The company, backed by Garnett Station Partners, targets established regional concepts with deep community ties and loyal customer bases. Its model gives acquired brands access to technology, data, analytics, and shared resources intended to support expansion without stripping away their local identities. “Our growth has always been deliberate,” ARB cofounder, chairman, and CEO Alex Macedo said in a statement. “We buy brands people love, we keep the operators who built them and we give them the tools to scale efficiently and thoughtfully. This capital lets us do more of that, faster.” Garnett Station formed ARB in 2021 through the acquisition of Primanti Bros., a Pittsburgh-based concept founded in 1933. The platform added P.J. Whelihan’s in 2022, Houston-based Mambo Seafood and Pollo Tropical parent Fiesta Restaurant Group in 2023, and Tavern in the Square parent Broadway Hospitality Group in 2024. Each of ARB’s five concepts has operated for more than 25 years. The portfolio spans several distinct geographic territories, including Florida, Texas, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Ohio, West Virginia, Massachusetts, Philadelphia, and South Jersey. Trimontium founder and chief investment officer Vlado Spasov described ARB as a high-quality restaurant business with a differentiated platform and a clearly defined expansion strategy. He also pointed to Garnett Station’s operating experience in foodservice as a key component of the transaction. Trimontium manages $1.6 billion in assets and provides flexible capital solutions to companies in Europe and North America. The firm is headquartered in London, maintains a presence in Luxembourg, and plans to expand into New York. Garnett Station, founded in 2013, manages approximately $4.5 billion in assets. Its primary investment categories include consumer and business services, health and wellness, automotive, and food and beverage. Simpson Thacher & Bartlett served as Trimontium’s legal adviser. Houlihan Lokey acted as valuation adviser, and La Presa Partners served as tax adviser. Kirkland & Ellis acted as ARB’s legal adviser, with Evercore serving as financial adviser. “Trimontium understood how we operate from the first conversation and structured their solution around what will support the business today,” Macedo said. “We are excited for this next chapter.” The post Primanti Bros. articles.title: After 10 Years of Sales Growth, The Melt Takes its Biggest Step Yet
articles.titleKo: After 10 Years of Sales Growth, The Melt Takes its Biggest Step Yet
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Melt has 24 locations. The Melt spent a decade proving it could transform its restaurants. Now it must prove someone else can run them just as well. The California-based fast casual is moving into franchising after lifting average unit volumes from $700,000 to roughly $3.5 million under CEO Ralph Bower. The growth plan calls for the company to reach 80 corporate restaurants by 2030 across California and Arizona, with franchisees carrying the brand into new states. It is a significant turn for a chain that was primarily known for grilled cheese when Bower arrived 10 years ago. The menu has since evolved into chef-inspired comfort food led by burgers, melts, mac and cheese, and chicken. The operating model has undergone an even larger transformation, producing 10 consecutive years of positive same-store sales and online ratings that have held between 4.7 and 4.8 this year. “I don’t know of another brand that’s ever been able to drive their AUVs from 700 [thousand] to 3.5 [million],” Bower says. His first move was to ask customers and employees what should change and what should stay. An email to the brand’s database drew 1,100 responses. Bower posed the same two questions to restaurant operators, collected the findings in a spreadsheet, and acted on the feedback. The resulting sales climb accelerated during the pandemic. Average unit volumes were near $1.5 million entering 2020 and doubled to $3 million by 2021. They have since gained another $500,000. The Melt’s sales initially fell 80 percent when shelter-in-place orders arrived in San Francisco, recovered to flat by May 2020 and set a record in June. Sales increased 57 percent from July through the end of that year, followed by a 54 percent gain in 2021 against the prior surge. The Melt had spent years preparing its kitchens to withstand high-volume periods. Its speed of service did not change by five seconds when sales doubled, Bower says. Proprietary software alerts restaurant personnel when ticket times breach key thresholds. A nine-minute average over a 15-minute window triggers texts to Bower, the chief operating officer, area manager, and general manager. A 15-minute mark prompts automated calls. Those peaks can arrive late. Forty percent of The Melt’s sales occur after 10 p.m. One San Francisco restaurant recently processed a $4,600 hour from 11 p.m. to midnight, following a $3,000 hour. A La Jolla store that routinely posted weekly sales near $20,000 before the pandemic reached $80,000 per week by the end of 2020. The brand ties employee bonuses to guest feedback and delivery errors instead of sales and profit. Operators join a 9 a.m. call seven days per week to review customer responses, mistakes, and restaurant performance. Teams also hold rallies before lunch and dinner shifts based on the companywide goal of delivering an “I love it here” experience to every guest. “I think sales and profits are what you did yesterday, what you did last week, and what you did last month. It’s history,” Bower says. “The number one indicator of what your success tomorrow is going to be is your guest feedback today.” The Melt’s franchising push will test whether that culture can transfer outside its corporate system. Bower has long been cautious of licensing the concept because he could not know how much of its improvement came from the food and how much came from operational intensity. Greg Vojnovic, head of franchising, began advising the company roughly a year ago. He and Bower previously worked together at Popeyes, and Vojnovic had evaluated two Melt sites years earlier. articles.title: Tijuana Flats Begins Next Chapter with Ambitious Franchise Push
articles.titleKo: Tijuana Flats Begins Next Chapter with Ambitious Franchise Push
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Tijuana Flats wants to be 80 percent franchised. Tijuana Flats is back in the franchising game. The brand relaunched its franchising program this spring following a turbulent stretch marked by bankruptcy, restaurant closures, and a change in ownership. Now, the 30-year-old chain is emerging from that reset period under the recently formed Latitude Food Group. Latitude was created after &pizza acquired Tijuana Flats last fall, forming a two-brand platform built around shared services and multi-brand franchising. The premise is to preserve the distinct personalities at the core of each concept while combining back-end resources to improve economics and create a more scalable foundation for operators. Tijuana Flats has taken a winding path through franchising. After beginning to franchise in the early 2000s, the brand halted new development in 2007 following a challenging early period and leaned more heavily on company-operated growth. It resumed a selective push in 2019, but that effort was paused a few years later. The company last filed its FDD in 2023, according to Latitude’s chief development officer Brett Willis. Tijuana Flats filed for bankruptcy in 2024 and closed dozens of restaurants. Under then-CEO Jim Greco, the company sought to stabilize operations, sharpen its positioning, improve menu offerings, and tighten restaurant-level costs. It emerged from bankruptcy in early 2025 before becoming part of Latitude later that year and officially relaunching franchising this spring. The immediate plan is twofold: refranchise select company-operated restaurants and pursue new development from both existing and prospective operators. Latitude is offering corporate stores in packages of three to five locations, with opportunities for larger packages, while conversations with existing Tijuana Flats franchisees are also underway. “Right now it’s heavily corporate owned,” Willis says. “We really want to take that more into a traditional franchising equation, meaning that 80 percent of the restaurants will be franchised and 20 percent will be corporate. We’ve kicked off an initiative alongside restarting our franchising program to sell some of our corporate shops to help spur some of that growth.” The company aims to sell about 20 restaurants this year—roughly 20 percent of the existing portfolio—and secure another 20 to 40 development commitments through a mix of new-build agreements and deals tied to refranchised locations. Initial development attention is centered on Florida and the broader Southeast, where Tijuana Flats has its deepest brand recognition and operating base. Latitude does not intend to eliminate its corporate footprint altogether. It expects to retain a core group of company-operated restaurants, particularly around its Orlando headquarters, to test new menu items, technology, and operational initiatives before expanding them throughout the system. For prospective franchisees, Latitude’s main selling point is the platform behind the brand. While &pizza and Tijuana Flats remain separate consumer-facing concepts, their parent company can consolidate purchasing, marketing, technology, training, HR, creative production, and vendor relationships. The goal is to lower recurring costs, strengthen support, and create more dollars for franchisees to either retain or reinvest in growth. “At the core, the shared-services model allows us to really leverage economies of scale, which ultimately result in better unit economics,” says CMO Sergio Perez. That can mean savings on everyday operating expenses or additional resources for revenue-driving initiatives such as loyalty, media, catering, and third-party delivery. The Simpsons Treehouse of Horror menu is available for a limited time beginning September 10 at participating Jack in the Box restaurants nationwide. Halloween in Springfield is taking over Jack in the Box. Jack in the Box is teaming up with The Simpsons to bring the iconic Treehouse of Horror specials from the screen to the drive-thru with a limited-time lineup featuring Krusty-inspired burgers, Forbidden D’oh!nut Holes, an all-new Spooky Simpsons Sauce, six special-edition glow-in-the-dark cups and custom packaging that brings Jack Box into the twisted world of Treehouse of Horror. Meet the Munchie Meal of Horror Leading the frightful feast is the Munchie Meal of Horror, summoned straight from Springfield as a terrifying twist on Jack’s legendary late-night meal. Fans can choose between a Double Krusty Burger of Terror or Double Chicken Sandwich of Terror, served alongside two tacos, seasoned curly fries and a drink. Each meal also comes with one of six special-edition glow-in-the-dark The Simpsons Treehouse of Horror cups and arrives in an exclusive Treehouse of Horror Munchie Meal box that brings Jack Box into the twisted world of Springfield. Both sandwiches feature the all-new Spooky Simpsons Sauce, a smoky BBQ ketchup created exclusively for the collaboration, and are served on custom sesame seed buns inspired by the burgers seen in the world of The Simpsons . More Ways to Get a Taste of Springfield Whether looking for a classic bite or something a little more monstrous, fans can also experience the collaboration through a lineup of The Simpsons Treehouse of Horror Meals, with four themed entrées to choose from. Each meal is served with fries and a drink, giving fans more ways to get a taste of Springfield: Krusty Burger of Terror: Terrifyingly delicious seasoned 100% beef patty, melty American cheese, lettuce, tomato, and new Spooky Simpsons sauce on a toasted sesame seed bun. Inspired by Homer famously selling his soul to the devil for a donut, these dangerously tempting bites are a treat worth risking it all for. Warm donut holes are dusted with cinnamon sugar, topped with pink frosting and finished with rainbow sprinkles for a Jack take on the iconic pink donut. Even the packaging gets in on the horror, featuring Homer’s unforgettable transformation into a donut straight from the classic segment. articles.title: Mountain Mike’s Pizza Opens in Georgetown, Texas
articles.titleKo: Mountain Mike’s Pizza Opens in Georgetown, Texas
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Mountain Mike’s Pizza, a leading family-style pizza chain for nearly 50 years, and home of the legendary crispy, curly pepperoni, massive 20-inch Mountain-sized pizzas and dough made fresh daily, is now open in Georgetown, Texas, marking the 17th location in the Lone Star State. The Georgetown restaurant is owned and operated by Rajeev Dewan, who owns two existing Mountain Mike’s locations in Manor and Cedar Park, and is actively developing two additional locations across Central Texas. For nearly five decades, Mountain Mike’s Pizza has delighted guests with “Pizza the Way it Oughta Be!” and is rapidly expanding into new markets across the country. Williamson County residents and visitors alike can enjoy the brand’s signature pizza experience at the new Mountain Mike’s in Georgetown, whether dining in, carrying out or via delivery. “As a business owner, I am deeply committed to creating lasting, meaningful connections with the local community, and Mountain Mike’s Pizza gives us the opportunity to bring families together while supporting local schools, first responders and youth programs that make Georgetown thrive,” said Dewan “Georgetown’s historic character, welcoming atmosphere and strong sense of community make it an exciting place to bring Mountain Mike’s, and we’re proud to join the growing local restaurant scene with ‘Pizza the Way It Oughta Be!’” The spacious 2,400-square-foot Mountain Mike’s Pizza in Georgetown features the welcoming, family-friendly atmosphere for which the brand is known. Boasting six big-screen televisions, the Georgetown restaurant is bound to be a go-to destination for sports fans, no matter which team guests root for. The Georgetown restaurant also includes a weekday all-you-can-eat pizza buffet and salad bar, an outdoor patio, kids’ arcade area and complimentary Wi-Fi. There is something for everyone at Mountain Mike’s in Georgetown, making it an ideal spot for guests of all ages, team parties, family get-togethers, office gatherings and group fundraising events alike. One bite into a cheesy slice of pizza from Mountain Mike’s takes you back to childhood, providing a sense of nostalgia for when pizzas were handmade with the freshest and finest ingredients. From its legendary crispy, curly pepperoni, 100% whole milk mozzarella cheese and a variety of fan-favorite specialty pizzas, Mountain Mike’s has something to satisfy every taste. Whether it’s dine-in, carryout or its own in-house delivery, guests can always count on Mountain Mike’s to ensure quality, freshness, flavor and value. Orders may be placed online, through the Mountain Rewards App or through any of the brand’s third-party delivery partners. The new Georgetown Mountain Mike’s is located at 1314 W University Ave., Suite 101, and can be reached by (512) 352-9888. The restaurant is open Sunday through Wednesday from 10:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. and Thursday through Saturday from 10:30 a.m. to 11 p.m. For additional information about Mountain Mike’s Pizza, visit www.mountainmikespizza.com. For additional information about the Georgetown location, visit Mountain Mike’s Georgetown/W. University Dr. or find the restaurant on Google and Yelp. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Buddy’s bar-b-q has spent more than 50 years serving up slow-smoked favorites across East Tennessee, and now the hometown staple is adding a crispy new option to the mix. New chicken tenders are officially on the menu, giving Buddy’s guests another affordable, family-friendly favorite alongside the bar-b-q, Southern sides and signature flavors they already know and love. Fried fresh and served hot, Buddy’s tenders feature juicy chicken hand-coated in a golden, crispy breading. Served plain, tossed in Buddy’s bar-b-q sauce or finished with Buddy’s signature seasoning for an extra kick — the new tenders bring a satisfying crunch and classic Buddy’s flavors to every bite. The tenders can be ordered à la carte in four- or five-piece portions, or as a combo with a drink and guests’ choice of side from Buddy’s classic Southern lineup. Four-piece orders start at $5.59 à la carte or $8.99 as a combo, while five-piece orders start at $6.59 à la carte or $9.99 as a combo. Guests can round out their chicken tender meal with comforting Southern sides, from savory Hushpuppies and Baked Beans to Coleslaw and Potato Salad. Each tender combo also comes with a choice of bar-b-q, ranch or honey mustard dipping sauce, adding an extra boost of flavor to every crispy bite. “Our guests have always trusted us to deliver quality food made simple at a great price, and we think these chicken tenders fit right in at Buddy’s,” said Mark Lemoncelli, CEO of Buddy’s bar-b-q. “Whether it’s an easy family dinner, a quick lunch or something the kids will love, we’re always looking for ways to give our guests more choices while staying true to what they’ve loved about Buddy’s for generations.” The new chicken tenders continue Buddy’s tradition of serving A Smokin’ Good Deal™, bringing an affordable, familiar favorite to the menu alongside the franchise’s signature bar-b-q offerings. With options for a quick bite, family meal or something in between, the tenders give longtime fans and new guests alike another way to enjoy the flavor and value Buddy’s has served for generations. With more than five decades of tradition behind it, Buddy’s continues to evolve its menu while staying rooted in the classic flavors, great value and Southern hospitality that have defined the brand since 1972. Buddy’s new chicken tenders are available now at all locations across East Tennessee. For more information on Buddy’s bar-b-q, please visit Buddysbarbq.com. For all media inquiries, please email PR@InnoVisionMarketingGroup.com. The post Buddy’s bar-b-q Adds Chicken Tenders to Menu appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Hyll Appoints David Kelman as Executive Chef
articles.titleKo: Hyll Appoints David Kelman as Executive Chef
articles.originalSummary: Cotswolds boutique hotel HYLL has appointed David Kelman as Executive Chef, bringing one of the region’s most respected culinary talents to lead the food offering at the new 17th century manor house hotel. Kelman joins HYLL following his role at Estelle Manor in Oxfordshire and brings more than two decades of experience across some of the UK’s most acclaimed country house hotels and hospitality destinations. Originally from North Wales, Kelman has built an impressive career spanning Bodysgallen Hall, Lower Slaughter Manor, Wyck Hill House, Ellenborough Park, Cowley Manor, Thyme and Burford Garden Company. He is particularly recognised for his tenure as Executive Head Chef at Ellenborough Park in Cheltenham, where he led the Beaufort Dining Room to three AA Rosettes and received numerous accolades, including Best Chef at the Taste of Gloucestershire Awards and Chef of the Year at the Cotswold Life Food & Drink Awards. A familiar face within the industry, Kelman represented Wales on BBC’s Great British Menu in 2014 and has cooked for members of the Royal Family, including Queen Elizabeth II and the then Prince of Wales. He has also represented Wales internationally as a member of the Welsh National Culinary Team. At HYLL, which opened in September 2025, Kelman will oversee the hotel’s culinary direction, developing menus that celebrate the seasons and the exceptional produce of the Cotswolds and surrounding counties. His approach centres on ingredient-led cooking, strong relationships with local suppliers and creating memorable dining experiences that reflect a genuine sense of place.

articles.title: Businesswoman Behind £20m+ London Hospitality Group Reveals New French Riviera Hotel and Art-Led Villa
articles.titleKo: Businesswoman Behind £20m+ London Hospitality Group Reveals New French Riviera Hotel and Art-Led Villa
articles.originalSummary: Former investment banking director Elmira Amdiy is expanding beyond her seven-strong London restaurant portfolio and existing French Riviera hotel, with a new hotel development and art-led villa on the Mediterranean coast. The businesswoman behind the Wild Group, the eight-figure hospitality group that includes some of London’s most coveted restaurants, including Belvedere, Wild Tavern, Wild Izakaya, Wild Corner, Wild Notting Hill, Chelsea Grill and Pinna Mayfair, has revealed the next stage of her wider hospitality portfolio, with two major projects underway on the French Riviera. Former investment banking director Elmira Amdiy, formerly of Barclays Capital, Nomura and UBS , is preparing to restore and redevelop a collection of historic buildings into a new hotel, named Hotel Les Chardons, while also creating a private seven-bedroom art villa at her existing luxury hotel, Hostellerie La Farandole. The villa is being created in partnership with renowned artist and sculptor Grishi Giano, who is designing the property in its entirety, from its recycled materials and interiors to original stone sculptures, creating a villa that will be a work of art in its own right . Meanwhile, plans for Hotel Les Chardons are taking shape , with Amdiy currently developing the concept around a potential focus on wellness and longevity . The historic buildings will be carefully restored and redeveloped, with architectural plans revealing landscaped gardens, restaurant terraces overlooking the French Riviera and a large outdoor swimming pool with an expansive poolside lounge area. Amdiy said: “Hotel Les Chardons is a significant project for us. We’re taking a collection of existing buildings and creating something new around them, while also being very conscious of what is already there and what we can restore. If we do take Les Chardons in the wellness and longevity direction, we will make sure there is real substance behind it, and a reason for people to travel specifically to stay with us. ” The projects mark a significant expansion of Amdiy’s hospitality interests beyond London, where she has spent the past five years working alongside her partners and team to build Wild Group from a single restaurant into a £20m+ portfolio spanning seven venues and employing more than 300 Londoners . Her involvement in hospitality began in France. Alongside her career in investment banking, Amdiy was already involved in the ownership of Hostellerie La Farandole before investing in Wild Tavern in 2020 and going on to help build the wider Wild Group portfolio. A SEVEN-BEDROOM VILLA CREATED AS A WORK OF ART The seven-bedroom private villa at Hostellerie La Farandole is on track for completion by the end of 2026, when it will become available to book through the hotel. Set within private grounds, the villa will have its own swimming pool and pétanque area . Amdiy is working closely with renowned artist and sculptor Grishi Giano on the design of the entire villa , with art and design being developed together from the outset. His involvement spans materials, furniture and lighting to original sculptures created specifically for the property and its grounds . Amdiy said : “I didn’t want us to design the villa and then decide what art to put on the walls afterwards. Grishi has been involved from the very beginning, so the art is part of the design rather than something added at the end. koreanSummary: Former investment banking director Elmira Amdiy is expanding beyond her seven-strong London restaurant portfolio and existing French Riviera hotel, with a new hotel development and art-led villa on the Mediterranean coast.

articles.title: Broadwick Soho in London’s West End joins Small Luxury Hotels of the World’s Finest Collection

articles.originalSummary: Small Luxury Hotels of the World (SLH) has welcomed Broadwick Soho as the first London hotel to join its Finest Collection, a selection of exceptional, independent properties recognised for their distinctive character, unmistakable sense of place and consistently outstanding guest experiences. Set in the heart of London’s West End, Broadwick Soho brings a bold, bohemian and deeply personal expression of luxury to the collection. The 57-room hotel channels the glamour, eccentricity and creative energy of its neighbourhood through richly layered interiors, characterful dining and an evolving cultural programme spanning art, music, design and performance. It’s a vibrant hub for local creativity, connection and community. Conceived by a group of friends and creatives, the property, located at 20 Broadwick Street, Soho is partly inspired by owner Noel Hayden’s childhood memories of his family’s flamboyant seaside hotel in Bournemouth. Internationally acclaimed interior architect Martin Brudnizki brought the vision to life in his first London hotel project, combining English eccentricity, Jazz Age opulence and disco-era glamour. A dynamic assortment of materials, colours, fabrics and textures have been used to create a whimsical and colourful menagerie, embodying 70s hedonism. Each room and suite has been meticulously designed, featuring bespoke furniture by Brudnizki, antiques and vintage curios. The hotel’s 10 suites and Penthouse are swathed in marbled wallpaper depicting floating elephants, tigers and exotic flora and fauna, complemented by handmade furniture such as custom minibars masquerading as brass elephants, made in Jaipur. The kaleidoscopic hotel is also home to more than 300 original artworks, bringing together internationally recognised names and emerging global artists. Highlights include works by Andy Warhol, Francis Bacon, Bridget Riley, Victor Pasmore, Faye Wei Wei and Casey Moore, alongside specially commissioned pieces created for the guestrooms and suites. A cultural address in the heart of Soho Broadwick Soho’s cultural programme further connects guests with Soho’s creative life. Since opening in November 2023, the hotel has hosted live performances from artists including Sister Sledge, Sheryl Crow, Sophie Ellis-Bextor and Dave Stewart, alongside DJs, emerging talent, talks and events linked to London Fashion Week, Pride in London and Frieze. During Frieze London from 15 to 18 October 2026, Broadwick Soho will host an artist residency centred around Moroccan multidisciplinary artist Rita Alaoui. The programme will combine an artist-led workshop with access to Frieze London, private gallery visits and intimate conversations with artists, collectors, curators and cultural figures. “Broadwick Soho is exactly the kind of hotel Small Luxury hotels of the World was created to celebrate – a small hotel with a big experience” said Richard Hyde, Chief Operating Officer at Small Luxury Hotels of the World. “It is independently minded, deeply personal and inseparable from the character of its location. Every element, from its design and art collection to its cultural programming and hospitality, reflects a confident and original point of view.” He continued, “Finest Collection brings together hotels that are destinations in their own right. articles.title: Tigermilk Brings Hacienda Grandeur to the Heart of East London
articles.titleKo: Tigermilk Brings Hacienda Grandeur to the Heart of East London
articles.originalSummary: Their modern South American inspired interior brings life to their largest site to dat e Following its successful opening in May, Tigermilk Spitalfields’s interior has emerged as one of the defining elements of the new flagship restaurant by Alexis and Nina Melikov, the group’s largest site to date. Designed by Studio Leche, Tigermilk’s in-house design studio, the space brings together hacienda-inspired architecture, layered materials and a warm, transportive atmosphere that has become central to the guest experience. Conceived as an escape in the heart of Spitalfields, the ambition was to build an environment that guests would immediately want to stay in, rather than one designed purely to be photographed. Central patios, generous proportions, fountains, handcrafted materials and lush greenery give the space its structure and soul, evoking the kind of environment that takes decades to settle into its surroundings. Antique furniture sits alongside bespoke pieces, and reclaimed terracotta, natural stone, marble and aged timber are used throughout, materials that carry history and wear it well. “People rarely talk about specific design features. They talk about the atmosphere,” adds Alexis. “If people leave believing the space possesses a history, then we have succeeded in creating something that feels authentic rather than constructed.” A considered selection of suppliers and craftspeople underpins the interior. Sogni and Pooky provide the lighting, Pierre Frey and Morris the fabrics and upholstery, and Mandarin Stone the marble and stone surfaces. Flexhouse – responsible for custom joinery, millwork and bespoke fabrication – also contributed to the furniture alongside vintage pieces and Leta, while Resources delivered the decorative wall finishes. Together they bring a layered quality to the space, as though each element has its own provenance and story. With its new 280-cover restaurant, hacienda-inspired interiors and striking luminescent bar stocked with more than 2700 bottles, Tigermilk Spitalfields invites guests into what feels like the brand’s thirteenth home. Through a considered interior scheme full of texture and attention to detail, the restaurant offers a transportive South American-inspired experience designed to engage every sense.

articles.title: The Flying Biscuit Café Opens in Knoxville, Tennessee
articles.titleKo: The Flying Biscuit Café Opens in Knoxville, Tennessee
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Flying Biscuit Café opens its downtown café at 327 W Summit Hill Dr SW in Knoxville, Tenn., on Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026, bringing the Atlanta-born breakfast and brunch brand into the city’s downtown core for the first time. The café is owned and operated by Chris Compton, who opened the brand’s first Tennessee location at 11683 Parkside Dr in the Turkey Creek area in May of 2025. Downtown is his second Flying Biscuit café. The space includes a patio and a full bar and covers 3,428 square feet with seating for 140. Compton expects to employ around 30 people at the location. Compton chose the Summit Hill Drive site for its position in the center of the city and its proximity to the University of Tennessee, where he swam as an 11-time All-American and SEC champion and was ranked among the top 10 swimmers in the world in 1992. He said the blocks around the café draw downtown office workers, state and city employees, and UT students through the week, with few sit-down breakfast options among them. Before moving into hospitality, Compton spent more than 20 years founding and running companies in credit card finance, real estate development and technology consulting. “Turkey Creek has been good to us, and the question we kept hearing was when we were coming downtown,” said Chris Compton, owner of The Flying Biscuit Café Knoxville. “There are a lot of people on these blocks by 8 a.m. and not many places to sit down and eat. Creamy dreamy grits, freshly baked biscuits, a rich pistachio latte and somebody glad to see you walk in — that’s what opens on Summit Hill on Sept. 12.” The Flying Biscuit Café Downtown Knoxville is at 327 W Summit Hill Dr SW, Knoxville, TN 37902, and opens to guests Saturday, Sept. 12. Hours are 7 a.m. to 2 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. Friday through Sunday, with dinner service from 5 to 9 p.m. Friday and Saturday. The café serves breakfast and lunch daily and offers full-service catering. Guest inquiries can go to knoxvilledowntown@flyingbiscuit.com and catering requests to knoxvilledowntowncatering@flyingbiscuit.com. The location phone is (865) 427-6748. Menus and location details are at flyingbiscuit.com. Compton’s Turkey Creek café remains open at 11683 Parkside Dr, Knoxville, TN 37934, (865) 288-0513. Compton plans to keep working with Knoxville-area nonprofits through the downtown café, continuing the partnerships he built around Turkey Creek. He plans to keep developing Flying Biscuit cafés in the greater Knoxville area over the next five years. Flying Biscuit Franchising is continuing to award territories across the Southeast and Texas including Tennessee, Kentucky, Florida, Virginia, Arkansas, and Ohio. Prospective operators can review open markets, ownership requirements and how to start a conversation with the development team at flyingbiscuitfranchising.com. articles.title: JOEY Restaurants Opens Second Dallas Location
articles.titleKo: JOEY Restaurants Opens Second Dallas Location
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . JOEY Restaurants, the award-winning, globally inspired hospitality group known for its elevated yet approachable culinary experiences, will open JOEY Maple, its second Dallas location, on Thursday, September 10. Located at 2508 Maple Avenue, the restaurant will offer a dynamic new destination for Uptown Dallas residents and visitors alike, serving lunch, happy hour and dinner. As part of the brand’s continued U.S. growth, JOEY Maple will bring the company’s signature blend of globally inspired cuisine, exceptional service and vibrant atmosphere to the neighborhood. “Uptown Dallas has one of the most energetic dining communities in the country, and expanding in Texas is a significant milestone for our brand, representing an exciting step in our growth strategy,” said Layne Krienke, president of JOEY Restaurants. “We designed JOEY Maple around a menu that gives guests a reason to keep coming back, from approachable favorites to globally inspired dishes and signature JOEY creations. Whether it’s a quick lunch or dinner that turns into drinks, the food is at the heart of the experience.” TOP CHEF TALENT, GLOBAL FLAVORS AND SIGNATURE SIPS At JOEY Maple, Executive Chef Matthew Stowe, a winning Top Chef alumnus and recent guest judge, will lead a menu that blends JOEY signatures with globally inspired flavors, bringing the brand’s distinctive approach to contemporary dining. The beverage program will be overseen by Bar Development Leader Jay Jones, a Restaurant Hall of Fame inductee, alongside Group Sommelier Jason Yamasaki. The menu reflects JOEY’s long-standing philosophy of blending global culinary techniques with high-quality ingredients showcasing a balance of premium steaks, fire-torched sushi, fresh seafood, bowls, handhelds and shareable plates. Guests can soon enjoy iconic cuts such as the Bone-In Prime Ribeye and Tomahawk, served with JOEY’s signature Crispy Mashed Potatoes alongside new dishes including Crispy Nigiri, Caviar, Truffle Udon Carbonara and JOEY Signature Chocolate Cake. The beverage program includes a curated wine list selected by Yamasaki and handcrafted cocktails from the Sarti Spritz and The Good Life Margarita, to the Woodsmoked Old Fashioned and JOEY Martini. Guests can also enjoy the JOEY Supers, a twist on the classic highball with its noteworthy lemon-lime slush. THOUGHTFULLY DESIGNED, INSPIRED TO CONNECT Designed as a modern, dynamic escape, JOEY Maple offers a comfortably elegant retreat in Uptown Dallas. The exterior establishes strong architectural presence through expansive floor-to-ceiling glazing, and sculptural vertical wood screening that softens the building’s profile. With over 7,800 square feet, the design centers around an immersive indoor alfresco environment, anchored by a fully operable skylight and perimeter operable windows, creating the sensation of dining outdoors while enjoying the comfort of the interior. Guests are welcomed by a fire bowl lounge surrounded by lush plantings and greeted by a sculptural curved millwork wine display to establish a strong sense of craftsmanship and hospitality. A signature statement light installation introduces a playful, artistic element that immediately defines the restaurant’s character. Guests will also delight in a gallery wall featuring one-of-a-kind works by America Martin, B Shawn Cox and James Wolanin. The collection is anchored by a custom commissioned piece from artist Mina Eskandari that pays homage to the site’s previous identity as a beloved day lounge and pool destination, celebrating the history of the location while giving it a contemporary new expression. Positioned as a focal point at the back of the restaurant, the open kitchen is celebrated with a dramatic lighting installation where the warm amber glow will draw guests through the space and enrich the dining atmosphere. The Village Dallas announces the appointment of Chef Eduardo Osorio as Culinary Director, expanding his leadership across the iconic Dallas community’s collection of restaurants, bars and entertainment destinations. In his new role, Osorio will oversee the culinary direction of Meridian, Over Under, Village Beach Club, Anise, Buzz & Bustle and future food and beverage initiatives throughout The Village. He will also continue serving as Executive Chef of Meridian. As Culinary Director, Osorio will collaborate with the culinary teams across The Village to guide menu development, maintain quality and consistency, mentor culinary talent and support the continued evolution of each concept’s culinary program. His leadership will support a cohesive food and beverage vision across the property while allowing each destination to retain their own distinct experience. “The Village is more than a place where people live and work—it is a destination where the Dallas community and visitors can come together to experience a diverse mix of dining, shopping, entertainment and hospitality,” said Osorio. “I’m excited to work alongside the talented teams at each culinary concept and continue raising the bar across the property. My goal is to create thoughtful, memorable experiences that feel true to each destination while strengthening the sense of connection and hospitality that defines The Village.” Osorio’s expanded role encompasses The Village’s diverse culinary portfolio, including: Meridian , The Village’s ingredient-driven, live-fire restaurant where Osorio will remain executive chef, creating seasonal dishes influenced by his coastal roots and global culinary experience. Over Under , a lively neighborhood sports bar offering classic American fare, drinks and an energetic setting for watching games and gathering with friends. Village Beach Club , a resort-style pool and entertainment destination featuring poolside dining, cocktails, live music and seasonal events. Anise , located at The Drey Hotel, contemporary neighborhood gathering place for breakfast and lunch by day and cocktails and evening bites by night in a warm, welcoming setting. Buzz & Bustle , The Village’s neighborhood coffee shop and daytime gathering place serving coffee, breakfast, lunch and grab-and-go selections. “Chef Eduardo has demonstrated an exceptional ability to pair culinary creativity with genuine hospitality and strong leadership,” said Brandy Spence, VP of Food & Beverage for The Village. “He understands that each of our concepts serves a different purpose while contributing to the larger experience of The Village. We are confident his vision, collaborative approach and commitment to quality will help our culinary program continue to evolve while remaining deeply connected to our residents, guests and the greater Dallas community.” Born in Los Angeles, Osorio has built a dynamic culinary career shaped by coastal influences, global experiences and a deep respect for thoughtful hospitality. He began his career in Marina del Rey and Santa Monica, where he developed an early appreciation for seasonal ingredients, sustainable seafood and the vibrant flavors of California’s coastal dining scene. His culinary journey has since taken him through some of the world’s most diverse food destinations, including New York, Chicago, Saudi Arabia, Las Vegas and Dallas. Working across an array of cultures, kitchens and dining environments has broadened his perspective and refined his approach to food, leadership and service. At Meridian, Osorio brings those influences together through intentional, ingredient-driven cooking grounded in a strong sense of place. His approach balances creativity with accessibility, allowing the quality of each ingredient to remain at the forefront while introducing guests to thoughtful flavor combinations and techniques. articles.title: Flame Broiler Launches New Nonprofit Foundation
articles.titleKo: Flame Broiler Launches New Nonprofit Foundation
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Flame Broiler, the family-owned quick-service restaurant brand known for its Korean-inspired rice bowls, announces the launch of the Flame Broiler Foundation , the company’s new philanthropic arm dedicated to supporting and feeding under-resourced youth and communities. The Foundation marks a new chapter in the brand’s legacy on the heels of its 30th anniversary and begins with a new round up campaign. For the month of September, guests can round up their change to the nearest dollar or donate any additional amount at checkout, both online and in-store at participating locations. To make the most impact, Flame Broiler has underwritten all operational overhead costs so that 100% of proceeds will benefit nonprofit organizations dedicated to the Foundation’s mission: to promote food equity and the betterment of communities. Flame Broiler Foundation will provide funding, meal donations and volunteer support to local organizations that deliver after-school programming, community enrichment and healthy meal programs. This work will be defined by three key priorities: promoting youth food equity, empowering community development and transforming food systems. The Foundation has supported around 400 youth through grants and in-kind donations to after-school and summer programs for at-risk students, foster youth, family services, workforce development and more. The Lee family, founders Young and Sarah, along with their sons Daniel, Christian and David, continue to lead the business that now spans two generations. The Foundation represents the family’s continued commitment to breaking down barriers for nutritious food, beyond the four walls of the restaurants. “Feeding communities was why we started Flame Broiler to begin with,” said Christian Lee, president and chief operating officer of Flame Broiler. “Thirty years later, we’re proud to carry on that same spirit, while expanding our impact through the Flame Broiler Foundation, ensuring philanthropy remains at the heart of our business.” The California-born brand continues to collaborate with local organizations such as longtime partners like OC United and new partners like Crece Urban Farms to help meet immediate needs of the community. Previous giveback has included delivering thousands of nutritious school lunches and supporting first responders through meal donations. “We believe that everyone, regardless of their background or location, should have the ability and opportunity to access and consume healthy, affordable and culturally connected foods,” said Asako Lee, executive director, The Flame Broiler Foundation. “We’re committed to advancing food equity and inspiring healthier communities for the next generation and the round up campaign is our first step – giving our guests a simple way to take part in our mission.” In-store and online rounding will run throughout the month of September at all corporate locations in California and participating franchisee locations. Customers across the country can participate when ordering online or through the Flame Broiler Magic Rewards app. To learn more, visit www.flamebroilerfoundation.org. Lou Malnati’s Pizzeria is celebrating football season with the return of its fan-favorite BuffaLou Chicken Pizza and a new Lou’s Rewards promotion rewarding loyalty members with free wings every time they order on game day and their market’s qualifying professional football team wins. The limited-time pizza is topped with Lou’s handcrafted wing sauce, made from a proprietary blend of homemade ranch dressing and Frank’s RedHot Original Cayenne Pepper Sauce. It’s built on Lou Malnati’s signature buttery, flaky crust, finished with Wisconsin mozzarella, premium all-white meat chicken, red onion and fresh parsley. Beginning Sept. 10, BuffaLou is available in both deep dish and thin crust for dine-in, carryout and delivery at all Lou Malnati’s locations, and ships nationwide for a limited-time through TastesofChicago.com. The pizza’s return comes alongside a new way for football fans in two of the company’s markets to celebrate a win. Starting with the season opener on Sept. 13, Lou’s Rewards members are automatically eligible for the promotion when they order on a qualifying game day in their market: games involving Chicago’s professional football team at Chicagoland locations, and games involving Chicago’s or Arizona’s professional football team at Arizona locations. When the qualifying team wins, a reward posts to the member’s account the next day, a free medium order of wings with any $30 purchase, redeemable within seven days. The promotion spans all game days each market’s qualifying teams are scheduled to play, keeping loyalty members engaged with Lou Malnati’s throughout the football season. “Guests have been asking us to bring BuffaLou back, and football season felt like the perfect time,” said Julie Younglove-Webb, CEO of Lou Malnati’s. “Lou’s has always been about bringing people together, whether it’s a family gathering or a game day watch party. Our new limited-time offering and Lou’s Rewards promotion carries that spirit forward, giving fans more reasons to come together and celebrate on game day. Order the BuffaLou to cheer on your team, then come back for free wings when they win.” For more information on BuffaLou Chicken Pizza, visit loumalnatis.com. articles.title: Wings Etc. Launches Ranch Flights with Five Flavors
articles.titleKo: Wings Etc. Launches Ranch Flights with Five Flavors
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Wings Etc. is adding a new sauce presentation to the menu with a Ranch Flight launching Tuesday, Sept. 15. The limited-time offer introduces two new ranch flavors — for a total of five — and a three-sauce presentation designed to encourage flavor sampling, customization and incremental sales. With the Ranch Flight guests can choose any three dips from the brand’s five house-made ranch flavors, including House Ranch, Ranch Fire, Parmesan Garlic Ranch and the brand-new Buffalo Ranch and Dill Ranch. The menu innovation expands the ways guests can dip, dunk, mix, match and customize their meals with Wings Etc.’s Big Flavor. The promotion also introduces a new presentation format for Wings Etc.’s sauces. Wings Etc. has invested in a new melamine serving tray for dine-in orders designed to enhance the overall in-store presentation compared with serving sauces in individual 2 oz. portion cups. Beyond presentation, the new tray makes it easier for guests to sample and compare three flavors at once and mix flavors for complete personalization. It offers a way for guests to amplify any menu item, from wings to burgers, sandwiches and fries — even pizza. “The Ranch Flight encourages guests to sample, compare and discover their favorite,” said Wings Etc. COO Chuck Moore. “Instead of simply serving dipping sauces, we’re creating an interactive flavor experience that serves up excitement.” The expanded lineup of ranch-inspired flavors and the launch of a Ranch Flight reflects Wings Etc.’s commitment to Big Flavor. In addition to the timeless House Ranch; the bold and adventurous Ranch Fire; and the rich and savory Parmesan Garlic Ranch, Wings Etc. is introducing two new ranch sauces: Dill Ranch starts with fresh dill finely chopped in-house. It’s stirred into classic ranch dressing with a splash of pickle juice for a bright, herb-forward dip that pairs perfectly with wings, wraps and sandwiches. Buffalo Ranch blends the cool creaminess of ranch dressing with the tangy heat of Wings Etc.’s signature Buffalo flavor — another top sauce among Wings Etc. guests — creating a perfectly balanced bit of kick for wings, tenders and fries. “Our objective is simple: When guests think about ranch, we want Wings Etc. to be the first brand that comes to mind,” said Moore. “By establishing our dominance with five ranch flavors and the Ranch Flight, we can create a unique competitive advantage, drive additional attachment sales, strengthen our flavor leadership and deliver an experience that guests can’t find anywhere else.” Wings Etc.’s investment comes as ranch grows in broad consumer appeal. It was one of the most talked about flavors around the globe during the FIFA World Cup, rivaling hydration breaks for online buzz. 1 But it’s been a favorite condiment nationwide for years. 2 According to Datassential, 3 75 percent of Americans like it or love it, more than any other dressing, and 44 percent of consumers have ranch weekly. “We know how much our guests love ranch — it’s our top-selling dip,” said Wings Etc. CEO Rob Hensmann. “As the Ranch Authority, we give fans more of the Big Flavor they crave, with fresh new varieties and the ability to personalize our award-winning wings as well as any menu item.” The Ranch Flight is a limited-time offer available in all markets. It will be served in a melamine tray for dine-in orders; carryout and delivery flights will be served in three 2 oz. cups. Pricing for the add-on is $2.69 to $2.99, depending on market. Fall flavors are here and football is back – and Krispy Kreme is making both even sweeter. Beginning Thursday, Sept. 10, fans can enjoy the NEW Apple Cider Original Glazed Doughnut and a Fall & Football Dozen made for game day gatherings, watch parties and all the delicious moments of the season. And there’s an even sweeter reason to huddle up: for four days only, Sept. 10 through 13, guests can score a dozen Apple Cider Original Glazed Doughnuts for just $5 with the purchase of any dozen at regular price at participating Krispy Kreme shops. Following the success of Krispy Kreme’s Original Glazed Blueberry Flavored Doughnut offered in July, the new Apple Cider Original Glazed Doughnut brings another craveable seasonal flavor to Krispy Kreme’s signature glaze. Made with apple cider dough, spiced with cinnamon and finished with Krispy Kreme’s iconic glaze, it delivers the warm, nostalgic taste of apple cider in every bite. Krispy Kreme is also getting into the game with the new Fall & Football Dozen, a lineup of four fan-favorite doughnuts to celebrate kickoff of the football season. 4 Football Doughnuts – a football-shaped unglazed shell filled with smooth, white Kreme, dipped in chocolate icing and finished with white icing football laces. 3 Pumpkin Spice Cake Doughnuts – an Original Glazed® Old Fashioned cake doughnut featuring pumpkin spice flavor. 2 Maple Cheesecake Doughnuts – an unglazed shell doughnut filled with cheesecake Kreme, dipped in maple icing and topped with graham-flavored crunch and maple drizzle. 3 Original Glazed® Doughnuts – Krispy Kreme’s iconic Original Glazed® Doughnut, hot, fresh and melt-in-your-mouth delicious. “Fall is full of rituals people look forward to – apple cider, game day, watch parties and sharing moments with friends,” said Alison Holder, Chief Product and Brand Officer at Krispy Kreme. “With Apple Cider Original Glazed and our Fall & Football Dozen, we’re giving fans a delicious new way to celebrate the season, whether they’re heading to a tailgate or settling in for kickoff.” The Apple Cider Original Glazed Doughnut and Fall & Football Dozen join Krispy Kreme’s Autumn Seasonal Collection , introduced in August and featuring seasonal doughnuts and beverages inspired by the flavors and comforts of fall. articles.title: bellagreen Launches Fall Seasonal Menu
articles.titleKo: bellagreen Launches Fall Seasonal Menu
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . bellagreen, the Dallas-based fast-casual restaurant known for made-from-scratch, healthy food, is launching its fall seasonal menu . Available at its Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston and San Antonio locations through Dec. 1, the menu brings the season’s flavors to the table with slow-simmered soup, roasted vegetables and three pumpkin dishes, savory and sweet. Every dish on the menu is gluten-free. Now Trending: Savory Pumpkin bellagreen looks beyond lattes and pie, incorporating nutrient-dense pumpkin in healthful, hearty dishes, including: Pumpkin Beef Chili – ground beef simmered with pumpkin puree, onions, bell peppers, carrots and warm spices, topped with sour cream, jalapeño and shredded cheese GF 4.99 / 6.99 Seared Salmon with Pumpkin Sauce – pan-seared salmon topped with a house-made creamy pumpkin sauce, served over rice pilaf with butternut squash and carrots GF 19.99 Nature’s Harvest Salad – spring greens, roasted butternut squash, red roasted beets and quinoa tossed in fig balsamic dressing, finished with goat cheese and toasted pumpkin seeds GF 14.99 Golden Glow Roasted Veggie Bowl – a returning favorite from the Winter Golden Glow menu, with quinoa, kale, roasted sweet potatoes and cauliflower, avocado, pumpkin seeds and a golden tahini-sriracha drizzle. GF 11.99 Add protein: +4.99 grilled or blackened chicken or tofu, +6.99 grilled or blackened shrimp or salmon Golden Glow Chicken Soup – slow-simmered chicken infused with turmeric, ginger, garlic, onions, tender sweet potatoes and carrots, with a touch of cream, finished with fresh herbs. GF 4.99 / 6.99 Pumpkin Cheesecake – creamy pumpkin cheesecake spiced with cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and clove, poured over a flaky, coconut hemp crust GF | VEG 7.49 / 45 “Pumpkin is more than a latte flavor. It’s one of the most nutrient-dense ingredients we get to cook with all year,” said bellagreen President Beth Collins. “It’s loaded with fiber and vitamin A, and it works just as well in a bowl of chili as it does in coffee or dessert. That’s what keeps our customers coming back each fall for this unique and healthy menu.” Gluten-Free, Not an Afterthought With Celiac Awareness Day on Sept. 13 , bellagreen’s fall menu offers a timely example of what happens when gluten-free diners get more than one or two options. Every fall dish is made without gluten from the start, even dessert. The seasonal menu features Pumpkin Cheesecake, made with a coconut hemp crust. “We have gluten-free options, but it goes well beyond that,” said Collins. “We’ve built a menu with a wide range of choices for guests with different dietary needs and preferences, including dairy-free and plant-based options. To us, hospitality means every guest should be able to walk in, find something they’re genuinely excited to eat and feel like the menu was built with them in mind – not like they’re settling for a workaround.” For more information or to view the full menu, visit bellagreen.com. Bubbakoo’s Burritos, the Jersey Shore-born Mexican-fusion brand known for bold flavors and fully customizable creations, is kicking off fall and the return of professional football with two new menu additions and a can’t-miss deal buy one, get one deal on entrées. Beginning Tuesday, September 8, guests can try Bubbakoo’s new Fried Cauliflower, available as both a starter and a protein option for customizing their favorite entrées, along with new Apple Pie Egg Rolls, a sweet addition arriving just in time for fall. The new offerings give guests even more ways to make their Bubbakoo’s experience their own, whether adding Fried Cauliflower to a favorite burrito, bowl, taco or quesadilla or finishing their meal with the warm, craveable flavors of Apple Pie Egg Rolls. Bubbakoo’s loyalty members will have an added reason to try something new, earning 15 bonus BubbaKoin the first time they purchase one of the new menu items. “We listen closely to what our guests love, and Fried Cauliflower has consistently been a fan favorite,” said Alex Jano, Vice President of Marketing at Bubbakoo’s Burritos. “Football season felt like the perfect time to bring it back—whether guests enjoy it as a shareable starter or use it to create their own bold, customized entrée. Together with our new Apple Pie Egg Rolls and football promotions, it delivers the fun, flavor and unexpected twists that define Bubbakoo’s.” The celebration continues September 9 when Bubbakoo’s invites fans to get amped for the kickoff of professional football season with a Buy One Entrée, Get One Free offer from 4 p.m. to close. Available in-restaurant and online with code “ SCORE”, guests can grab their favorite Bubbakoo’s entrée and score another on the house while settling in for the return of football. The offer is limited to one redemption per guest, applies to single-protein entrées, and has a maximum redemption value of $13.99. And the kickoff deal is just the start of Bubbakoo’s football season lineup. Every Sunday, loyalty members can earn 3X BubbaKoin. For watch parties, team gatherings, office lunches and other fall get-togethers, guests can also receive 15% off catering throughout September with code FEED15. Following years of impressive growth, Bubbakoo’s Burritos has established a prominent U.S. presence across the country, creating a dedicated legion of fans. Since its inception in 2008, Bubbakoo’s has grown from its Jersey Shore roots to more than 140 locations across 16 states. The brand has been recognized among Entrepreneur’s Franchise 500, QSR Magazine’s Top 50 Contenders, and the Inc. 5000 list of the fastest-growing private companies in America. Bubbakoo’s Burritos has been a Mexican-fusion staple in many communities since the brand’s inception in 2008. Featuring a variety of unique, customizable and wow-worthy menu items made-to-order with fresh ingredients, the brand has grown from its Jersey Shore roots and expanded to more than 100 locations across the United States.
