articles.title: Del Taco Expands Catering Business as Part of Comeback Plan
articles.titleKo: Del Taco Expands Catering Business as Part of Comeback Plan
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Del Taco, the nation’s second-largest Mexican quick service restaurant*, is expanding its catering business beginning Thursday, September 3. The initiative is the latest Project Del Sunrise milepost and provides guests with a more direct way to place Del Taco catering orders. The program also introduces Taco Salads to the catering menu and folds the brand seamlessly into workplace lunches, meetings, celebrations and other group occasions. Project Del Sunrise was announced earlier this year as a strategic roadmap to strengthen restaurant performance, expand guest occasions and drive long-term growth. As part of the revamped catering experience, guests can now explore and place catering orders through the Del Taco website. Previously, guests were directed to a third-party ordering platform. The new first-party experience gives Del Taco and its restaurants greater ownership of the catering relationship and creates a better way for guests to discover and order from the expanded menu. The change also provides new back-of-house tools for Del Taco operators to manage and deploy their catering orders. “Our menu works extremely well for group orders, and our catering relaunch supports an improved sales channel for our restaurants and franchise partners, while creating a significant opportunity to be part of occasions where Del Taco has historically had a limited presence,” said Ulyses Camacho, Chief Transformational Officer of Del Taco. “Catering was one of several key areas identified as part of Project Del Sunrise, and this relaunch is another example of turning strategy into action.” The expanded catering menu offers a range of options for individual meals and larger groups, including tacos, Epic Burritos and now, Taco Salads. Guests can choose from Individual Meals featuring tacos, Epic Burritos or Taco Salads; Burrito Boxes with Classic or Epic Burritos; and a Buffet Style Taco Kit with a choice of proteins. Taco Salads are available with Seasoned Beef, Grilled Chicken or Carne Asada Steak, giving groups another customizable option alongside Del Taco’s signature tacos and burritos. “Project Del Sunrise was initiated to find new avenues to grow the business and give guests more reasons to choose Del Taco,” Camacho added. “Catering is another important piece of that strategy, allowing us to bring the Del Taco experience into more moments that bring people together.” The catering relaunch is the first step toward a more fully developed Del Taco catering platform. Additional enhancements, including updated packaging, promotions and advertising, are planned as the brand continues to develop the channel. Starting Thursday, September 3, guests can explore catering options and place orders through www.deltaco.com/catering. For more information and to find the nearest Del Taco location, visit www.deltaco.com. *By number of units. articles.title: Maepole to Open First Drive-Thru Store in Cumming, Georgia
articles.titleKo: Maepole to Open First Drive-Thru Store in Cumming, Georgia
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Maepole, the Athens-born fast-casual restaurant putting a fresh, modern spin on Southern comfort food, will open its first standalone restaurant with a drive-thru pickup lane in Cumming later this year, marking a major step in the Georgia brand’s plans for regional growth. Maepole’s expansion is backed by Tony Townley, co-founder of Zaxby’s and a principal investor in the company. Townley brings decades of experience building and scaling restaurant concepts as Maepole develops its platform for regional and franchise growth. Located at the intersection of Bethelview Road and Castleberry Road, the new restaurant will introduce a purpose-built Maepole prototype featuring a full dining room, outdoor patio and the brand’s first drive-thru pickup lane. The format is designed to serve as a model for future company and franchise locations as Maepole expands throughout Georgia and, ultimately, the Southeast. “Cumming has the combination we look for in a Maepole community— growing families, active lifestyles and people who want better everyday food without sacrificing convenience,” said Chef Peter Dale, Maepole founder and Culinary Director. “We want to be just as useful on a busy Tuesday night as we are for lunch on Saturday. Sometimes that means sitting down with your family, and sometimes it means picking up a great meal on your way home.” Maepole describes its approach simply: a fresh, modern take on Southern specialties. The chef-driven menu takes the flavors, ingredients and hospitality associated with Southern food and reimagines them for the way people eat today. Guests build their own bowls from a selection of never frozen, scratch-made bases, vegetables, proteins and sauces, creating anything from a hearty comfort-food meal to a lighter lunch or protein-packed post-workout dinner. At the center of the concept is a belief that food can be both craveable and something guests feel good about eating. “Healthy food shouldn’t taste like a compromise,” Dale said. “We start with flavor and real cooking. We just happen to build those flavors around fresh vegetables, quality proteins and food we prepare from scratch every day. That’s been the idea behind Maepole from the beginning.” That approach also makes the menu accessible to a wide range of dietary preferences. Maepole offers extensive gluten-free, vegan and keto-friendly choices, features hormone- and antibiotic-free meats, and operates a 100% peanut- and tree-nut-free kitchen. The Cumming restaurant will be Maepole’s fourth Georgia location, joining two restaurants in Athens and one in Atlanta’s Summerhill neighborhood. The company is developing additional Georgia locations as it builds a repeatable standalone restaurant model designed to support future regional and franchise growth. This opening also represents an evolution in how guests can use Maepole throughout the day. In addition to dine-in service, guests will be able to order ahead and pick up meals through the dedicated pick-up lane, making the restaurant convenient for workday lunches, post-workout meals and weeknight family dinners. Maepole Cumming is expected to open in late 2026 at Bethelview Road and Castleberry Road in Cumming, Georgia, and will be its fourth Georgia location, joining its two Athens restaurants and its Atlanta location in Summerhill. For menu information and updates on the Cumming opening, visit Maepole.com. The post Maepole to Open First Drive-Thru Store in Cumming, Georgia appeared first on QSR Magazine .

A planning application submitted to Lambeth Council seeks permission to add a glazed veranda with a retractable roof around the existing terrace at Unit 14, Royal Festival Hall. The move would follow Dishoom’s opening at Battersea Power Station in 2023 and comes as the group also prepares to open in Borough. The South Bank application is still awaiting a decision and is supported by plans, rendered elevations and supporting heritage and flood-risk documents. - Stoke Newington’s Sonora Taqueria announced that it will close at the end of October, despite the owners describing the past year as their most successful to date. Husband and wife duo Michelle Salazar de la Rocha and Sam Napier revealed the restaurant’s final service will be on 31 October, after which they will take an indefinite break from the business. The pair acknowledged the decision may come as a surprise, but added that they have spent recent months stripping back parts of the taqueria that had become a burden and focusing on enjoying themselves. While they are unsure what comes next, they say they are excited about the future. - US restaurant brand Houston Hot Chicken has announced that it will open its second UK site at the Brunswick Centre in Bloomsbury, near Russell Square, this winter. The London opening will follow the brand’s first UK restaurant in Stevenage, which is due to open this autumn. The Nashville-style fried chicken concept will make its UK debut as part of Pizza Express’ plans to launch three Houston Hot Chicken sites this year and 50 over the next three years, following its acquisition of the brand’s UK franchise rights. Backed by restaurant-focused private equity firm Savory Fund, the chain specialises in hot chicken tenders, waffles, nuggets and sandwiches.

articles.title: Los Tacos No. 1 Lands Investment from TSG Consumer Partners
articles.titleKo: Los Tacos No. 1 Lands Investment from TSG Consumer Partners
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Los Tacos No. 1 has 10 locations in New York City. Los Tacos No. 1, a Mexican concept based in New York City, has secured a strategic investment from TSG Consumer Partners to support expansion. Financial terms were not disclosed. Cofounder and CEO Christian Pineda and chief operating partner Jacobo Ackerman will continue to lead day-to-day operations and strategic decisions. The company operates 10 locations across New York City, along with Los Mariscos, a sister seafood concept in Chelsea Market that serves Baja-style fish tacos, shrimp tacos, and ceviche. The partnership will provide resources and expertise to help Los Tacos grow and preserve its food and taco-shop experience. The announcement did not identify new markets or provide an opening timeline. TSG brings experience investing in growing restaurant brands. The private equity firm acquired a minority stake in Dutch Bros in 2018 and announced a minority growth investment in Pura Vida Miami in November 2025. Los Tacos was founded in 2013 by friends from Tijuana, Mexico, and Brawley, California, who wanted to bring the tacos they grew up eating to the East Coast. The brand opened its first stand in Chelsea Market, building its menu around family recipes, fresh ingredients, and Tijuana-style tacos served off the grill. The menu also features tostadas, quesadillas, and mulas with grilled steak, grilled chicken, marinated pork, or grilled cactus, plus a fried quesadilla. “When we moved to New York City, we couldn’t find good tacos that tasted like the ones we grew up with, so we set out to change that. Staying true to that has guided every decision as we’ve grown, and it’s why finding the right partner mattered so much,” Ackerman and cofounders Pineda, Tyler Sanders, and Kyle Cameron said in a joint statement. “TSG shares our belief that more cities deserve authentic tacos like these. They’ve spent decades working alongside founders, and that experience is exactly why we trust them for this next chapter. This is just the beginning.” East Wind Advisors served as exclusive financial advisor to Los Tacos. Davis Polk & Wardwell and Pryor Cashman provided legal counsel to the restaurant company, and Ropes & Gray represented TSG. Colin Welch, managing director and head of New York at TSG, pointed to the concept’s customer following as a foundation for expansion. “Christian, Tyler, Kyle, Ja and the entire team have created something rare and hard to build: a brand people feel a real connection to,” Welch said in a statement. “That’s the strongest possible foundation to grow from, and we couldn’t be more excited to help introduce Los Tacos No. 1 to more taco lovers.” The post Los Tacos No. 1 Lands Investment from TSG Consumer Partners appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Comment: Is Napoli on the Road’s pizza tasting menu a slice of genius?
articles.titleKo: Comment: Is Napoli on the Road’s pizza tasting menu a slice of genius?
articles.originalSummary: The Soho pizzeria’s new tasting menu gives one of the world’s most familiar foods a rethink. Pizza is generally a food that asks very little of its diners. It is familiar, comforting and, depending on the pizzeria, something to eat quickly and without too much thought. So, when I heard Napoli on the Road was launching a tasting menu, I was rather sceptical about how pizza would fit into the format. The £65 menu, created by chef Michele Pascarella, was launched at the group’s recently opened Soho restaurant as an attempt to reframe the modern pizzeria. However, the menu is not, Pascarella is keen to stress, an attempt to turn pizza into fine dining. Instead, it is an exploration of the format through ingredients, seasonality, memories and flavours. And while there is inevitably something of a publicity exercise about launching a tasting menu alongside a new restaurant, I found it an interesting way of testing how far pizza can be pushed before it stops feeling like pizza. The meal begins with tomatoes, prepared in four different ways and cooked for two, six and 10 hours. It is an unconventional opening and initially felt slightly at odds with the straightforward pleasure I normally associate with a pizzeria. But that is arguably the point. The tomatoes give you something to think about before the dough arrives, demonstrating how much variation can be extracted from a single ingredient. These tomatoes quickly became one of the focal points of the meal, prompting plenty of conversation not just around the table but long after the meal was over. Fritti follow, consisting of fried polenta, zucchini frittatina and a potato crocchè. all of which were perfectly enjoyable but felt less integral to the experience than what followed. While the plates were happily emptied, I doubt their absence would have been keenly felt.

articles.title: La Maritxu Launches in Selfridges Food Hall
articles.titleKo: La Maritxu Launches in Selfridges Food Hall
articles.originalSummary: La Maritxu, London’s much-loved Basque cheesecake brand, is delighted to announce its launch in the iconic Selfridges Food Hall. Customers can now discover and enjoy La Maritxu’s signature range of cheesecakes at one of London’s most celebrated food destinations. Founded in 2021 by husband-and-wife duo Ignacio and Lucia, La Maritxu has quickly developed a loyal following for its take on the traditional Basque cheesecake. The brand’s latest launch marks an exciting chapter, bringing its distinctive cheesecakes to Selfridges alongside some of the UK’s most exciting food and drink brands. Inspired by the cheesecakes of Bilbao, La Maritxu’s signature Basque-style cheesecake is baked at a high temperature to create its characteristic deeply caramelised, almost burnt top, while retaining a rich, smooth and creamy centre. The result is a cheesecake that is indulgent, distinctive and true to its Basque inspiration. Selfridges customers will be able to choose from a selection of La Maritxu favourites, including the Classic Cheesecake and Pistachio Cheesecake, alongside the Mango & Passionfruit Cheesecake, a limited-edition flavour. The cheesecakes are available in a range of sizes, from larger cakes designed for sharing to La Maritxu’s popular mini cakes priced at £14 each. The launch at Selfridges represents an exciting milestone for La Maritxu as the brand continues to grow its presence across London. With its distinctive Basque roots, high-quality ingredients and instantly recognisable caramelised finish, La Maritxu is bringing a taste of Bilbao to one of the capital’s most iconic food halls.

articles.title: Skechers muda estratégia no Brasil e prevê chegar a 100 lojas próprias
articles.titleKo: Skechers muda estratégia no Brasil e prevê chegar a 100 lojas próprias
articles.originalSummary: Terceira maior marca de calçados do mundo, com faturamento previsto de mais de US$ 10,5 bilhões neste ano, a Skechers planeja ampliar sua presença no Brasil e chegar a 100 lojas próprias nos próximos anos. Com cinco lojas instaladas nos estados de São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro e Minas Gerais, a companhia pretende dobrar sua operação até o final de 2026. A expansão brasileira faz parte da estratégia global da marca, que prevê aumentar sua rede de cerca de 5.300 para 10 mil lojas nos próximos anos. O plano de expansão começou a ser desenhado há cerca de um ano e meio, quando a matriz decidiu alinhar a operação brasileira aos padrões globais da marca. O processo exigiu uma revisão de processos internos, melhoria do catálogo de produtos e a contratação de uma equipe de liderança local. “O que fizemos, além de toda a infraestrutura interna e investimento, foi começar a abrir lojas. Já abrimos cinco lojas e colocamos o e-commerce no ar”, afirma Sabrina Mônaco, CEO da Skechers Brasil. Para iniciar este novo ciclo, a companhia investiu dezenas de milhões de reais, com recursos destinados a campanhas de marketing, aquisição de estoque, ampliação da estrutura de distribuição e um novo escritório corporativo em São Paulo, construído em menos de 65 dias. A companhia projeta dobrar o volume de negócios no Brasil a cada dois ou três anos. “Não trabalhamos com um teto de investimentos. O valor atual é o mínimo necessário para dar suporte ao negócio”, afirma David Weinberg, COO da Skechers. Os gargalos do passado Segundo Weinberg, o Brasil sempre esteve no radar da Skechers, que lidera as vendas no Chile e vem crescendo na Colômbia e no Peru. A expansão no mercado brasileiro, porém, foi adiada por alguns anos devido às particularidades do país. “No Brasil, a operação foi mais difícil por alguns fatores, como as regras de importação e os preços praticados na época, além da necessidade de desenvolver a produção local e entender melhor o mercado. Enquanto os negócios avançavam em outras partes do mundo, nunca houve dúvida de que o produto teria espaço no Brasil. A questão é que a empresa estava crescendo muito rapidamente em outros mercados e acabou adiando a expansão no País”, diz. Fora da América Latina, a prioridade estava na expansão da operação nos Estados Unidos, na Europa e na Ásia, que levou a companhia a direcionar investimentos para a construção de grandes centros de distribuição, o que reduziu o espaço para novos aportes no Brasil naquele momento. Três formatos de varejo físico e estreia no e-commerce As cinco unidades inauguradas no Brasil até agora estão divididas entre os formatos outlets, lojas Concept e as chamadas BBS ( Beautiful Big Big Stores ), unidades maiores e de rua, como as que a marca mantém em outros mercados. A próxima loja será aberta no Aricanduva, em São Paulo. A empresa também já tem contrato assinado para uma loja em Ribeirão Preto e mantém negociações para os demais endereços que completarão a rede prevista para este ano. Além das lojas físicas, a operação brasileira colocou no ar nesta semana uma plataforma de e-commerce integrada à tecnologia global da marca. Para disputar espaço com marcas esportivas já consolidadas no Brasil, a Skechers aposta na diversificação do portfólio. A estratégia segue o conceito de “supervia” (super highway), com atuação simultânea em dez divisões de produtos, que incluem desde corrida e basquete de alta performance até linhas infantis, trilha e moda casual. “Alguns dos concorrentes da Skechers são muito focados em uma única categoria. Eu gosto de usar uma analogia de que estamos na supervia. Se existem dez faixas, cinco indo em uma direção e cinco na outra, nós estamos em todas. Todas as categorias são importantes para a Skechers”, diz Michael Greenberg, presidente global da Skechers. articles.title: Quando o clima muda, o consumo também muda
articles.titleKo: Quando o clima muda, o consumo também muda
articles.originalSummary: O clima sempre fez parte da rotina do varejo, ainda que nem sempre tenha recebido a mesma atenção dedicada ao calendário promocional, aos preços ou às datas comemorativas. Mas, diante de fenômenos cada vez mais relevantes para o comportamento de consumo, como o El Niño , essa variável começa a ganhar outro peso nas decisões comerciais. E não estamos falando apenas sobre vender mais sorvete quando faz calor ou mais sopa quando esfria. Temperatura, chuva e eventos climáticos extremos interferem na forma como as pessoas se deslocam, nos horários em que compram, nos canais que escolhem, nas ocasiões de consumo e, consequentemente, nas categorias que ganham ou perdem relevância em determinados momentos. O El Niño é um bom exemplo dessa complexidade. O fenômeno altera os padrões de temperatura e precipitação em diferentes partes do mundo. No Brasil, seus efeitos também variam de acordo com a região, podendo favorecer volumes maiores de chuva no Sul e períodos mais secos e quentes em áreas do Norte e Nordeste. Para um país continental como o nosso, isso significa que o impacto sobre o varejo dificilmente será uniforme. Uma rede de supermercados com lojas em diferentes cidades ou estados pode encontrar, simultaneamente, consumidores vivendo contextos completamente distintos. Enquanto uma região enfrenta dias consecutivos de chuva, outra pode registrar temperaturas muito acima da média. E cada um desses cenários cria comportamentos e necessidades diferentes. É justamente aí que o clima deixa de ser apenas uma informação meteorológica e passa a ser uma variável de consumo. Um período de calor intenso pode aumentar a procura por bebidas geladas, sorvetes, água, frutas, protetor solar e itens associados ao consumo fora de casa. Mas também pode mudar os horários de maior fluxo da loja, estimular compras mais rápidas e alterar as ocasiões de consumo. A chuva produz outros movimentos. Dependendo da intensidade e da região, pode reduzir o fluxo físico, aumentar a relevância do delivery, favorecer compras de abastecimento e modificar o consumo de determinadas categorias. Existe ainda um efeito menos visível para quem olha apenas para dentro da loja: o clima também acontece antes da gôndola. Eventos climáticos interferem na produção agrícola, na disponibilidade de matérias-primas, na logística e nos custos de diferentes cadeias. Produtos frescos são especialmente sensíveis a essas oscilações, mas os reflexos podem chegar a muitas outras categorias. Em 2026, por exemplo, preocupações relacionadas ao El Niño já aparecem entre os fatores capazes de influenciar decisões da safra 2026/2027 e, consequentemente, preços e ofertas de alimentos. Isso cria um desafio importante para o varejo: o mesmo fenômeno pode mexer, ao mesmo tempo, com a oferta e com a demanda. O calendário comercial ganhou mais uma variável O varejo é extremamente competente em trabalhar calendário. Natal, Páscoa, Dia das Mães, férias, volta às aulas, verão, inverno e dezenas de outras datas ajudam a definir campanhas, compras, estoques, exposição e comunicação. O problema é que o calendário diz qual estação deveria estar acontecendo. O consumidor responde ao clima que realmente está vivendo. Um inverno com temperaturas elevadas pode frustrar uma estratégia construída meses antes para categorias tradicionalmente associadas ao frio. Da mesma forma, uma onda de calor fora de época pode criar uma oportunidade de venda que não estava prevista no planejamento original. Isso exige mais flexibilidade. Não significa abandonar o planejamento antecipado, mas criar uma operação capaz de reagir rapidamente quando o contexto muda. Rever exposição, comunicação, mídia, estoque, sortimento e até a intensidade promocional pode ser necessário quando o comportamento real começa a se distanciar daquele projetado. E existe aqui uma oportunidade especialmente interessante para supermercados. Poucos setores conseguem perceber mudanças de comportamento com tanta velocidade quanto o varejo alimentar. A freq

articles.title: Agentes de IA devem assumir etapas de busca, comparação e compra, aponta estudo
articles.titleKo: Agentes de IA devem assumir etapas de busca, comparação e compra, aponta estudo
articles.originalSummary: O próximo grande desafio do varejo digital pode não ser conquistar mais cliques, mas ser escolhido sem que o consumidor sequer visite o site da marca. É essa uma das mudanças estruturais apontadas pelo estudo “Futuros Conversacionais 2027 e 2028”, realizado pela WGSN e pela Blip. Segundo o estudo, a evolução da Inteligência Artificial deve levar a uma internet em que agentes pesquisam, interpretam informações e tomam decisões em nome dos usuários, reduzindo a necessidade de navegação tradicional. Mas a transformação vai além da já conhecida possibilidade de delegar compras a agentes de IA. O que muda é a própria arquitetura do comércio digital: sites, aplicativos e canais deixam de ser necessariamente o destino final da jornada e passam a funcionar também como fontes de informação e serviços que precisam ser compreendidos pelas máquinas. Esse cenário cria uma nova disputa para as marcas. Não basta estar presente na internet ou aparecer nos resultados de busca. Será necessário estruturar produtos, preços, estoques, políticas, serviços e informações de maneira que agentes de inteligência artificial consigam interpretar, comparar e executar ações a partir desses dados. Do SEO para a “legibilidade” das máquinas Durante anos, a lógica do comércio digital foi construída para conquistar o consumidor por meio de páginas, anúncios, mecanismos de busca e interfaces. A próxima etapa pode deslocar parte dessa disputa para os próprios sistemas de IA. O estudo aponta a evolução do modelo B2AI2C (Business to AI to Consumer), no qual agentes passam a ocupar uma posição intermediária entre empresas e consumidores. Nesse ambiente, uma marca pode não ter contato direto com o cliente durante toda a jornada. Isso muda a lógica de descoberta. Um agente pessoal poderá consultar diferentes empresas, cruzar informações, avaliar alternativas e apresentar ao usuário uma recomendação já filtrada. Para participar dessa jornada, a empresa terá de oferecer dados estruturados e serviços acionáveis por sistemas externos. APIs, autenticação, autorização, integração de sistemas e confiança deixam de ser apenas questões técnicas e passam a fazer parte da estratégia comercial. A2A: empresas negociando com agentes Uma das evoluções previstas é a comunicação entre agentes, o chamado Agent-to-Agent (A2A). De um lado, estarão agentes pessoais, capazes de representar preferências, interesses e dados do consumidor. Do outro, agentes das próprias empresas, conectados a estoque, preços, produtos, logística e atendimento. A consequência é uma mudança importante: o consumidor pode deixar de ser o único interlocutor da compra. Em determinadas jornadas, a negociação ocorrerá entre sistemas antes que uma decisão chegue à pessoa. A marca, portanto, precisará convencer não apenas o consumidor, mas também o agente responsável por interpretar suas necessidades e avaliar as alternativas disponíveis. A marca pode deixar de ser uma interface O avanço dessa lógica também coloca em xeque o papel atual de sites e aplicativos. Eles continuarão existindo, mas podem deixar de ser o principal ponto de contato em determinadas categorias. Em vez de abrir uma página, comparar dezenas de produtos e concluir a compra, o consumidor poderá expressar uma necessidade e receber uma solução já processada por seu agente. A consequência para as empresas é profunda: a experiência de marca terá de funcionar mesmo quando o consumidor não estiver olhando para a marca. Preço, disponibilidade, reputação, atributos do produto, políticas de troca, prazo de entrega e capacidade de atendimento poderão ser interpretados por sistemas antes de aparecerem para o usuário. articles.titleKo: Shein celebra fim da taxa das blusinhas; indústria têxtil critica
articles.originalSummary: A Shein celebrou a aprovação, pelo Congresso Nacional, da Medida Provisória 1.357/2026 , que mantém zerado o Imposto de Importação sobre compras internacionais de até US$ 50, a chamada taxa das blusinhas. A proposta foi aprovada pelo Senado nesta quinta-feira, 3, após passar pela Câmara e pela comissão mista, e agora segue para sanção presidencial. Segundo Felipe Feistler, country manager da Shein no Brasil, a decisão representa uma vitória para os consumidores brasileiros e contribui para ampliar o acesso a produtos de diferentes categorias. “Esta é, acima de tudo, uma grande vitória para o consumidor brasileiro. Parabenizamos o Congresso Nacional pela aprovação de uma medida que protege o poder de compra da população e amplia o acesso a produtos de qualidade, a preços acessíveis e a uma maior diversidade de oferta, especialmente para as famílias de menor renda”, afirmou. Indústria têxtil critica decisão A Associação Brasileira da Indústria Têxtil e de Confecção ( Abit ) criticou a aprovação da chamada MP das Blusinhas pelo Congresso Nacional. Em posicionamento divulgado após a votação, o setor classificou a medida como um “grave retrocesso” e afirmou que a decisão amplia a diferença competitiva entre empresas brasileiras e produtos importados. Segundo a entidade, a manutenção do Imposto de Importação zerado para compras internacionais de até US$ 50 cria um tratamento favorecido aos produtos estrangeiros, enquanto empresas instaladas no País continuam sujeitas a impostos, custos e obrigações. O setor afirma que os efeitos da medida já podem ser observados na queda da produção, no fechamento de postos de trabalho e na redução dos investimentos. Também aponta possíveis impactos sobre a arrecadação e a capacidade de manutenção da base industrial e comercial brasileira. A entidade argumenta que a discussão não deve ser tratada como uma disputa entre consumidores e produtores, mas como uma questão de igualdade de condições para competir. Para o setor, a redução da tributação sobre produtos importados pode gerar um benefício imediato ao consumidor, mas produzir efeitos negativos sobre emprego, renda e consumo no País. Outro ponto levantado pela indústria é o avanço da produção asiática. Segundo o posicionamento, grandes produtores da região, beneficiados por incentivos e subsídios, enfrentam excesso de capacidade produtiva e buscam novos mercados para seus produtos. O setor também afirma que o Brasil estaria seguindo uma direção diferente de outros países ao manter a isenção do Imposto de Importação para pequenas encomendas internacionais. “Não somos contra o comércio internacional, as plataformas digitais ou a evolução tecnológica. Defendemos a concorrência, mas concorrência com igualdade de regras. A indústria e o varejo brasileiros não pedem privilégios: exigem apenas o direito de competir em condições justas”, afirmou a entidade. Apesar da aprovação da medida, o setor declarou que continuará atuando contra o que considera uma desigualdade concorrencial e em defesa de condições consideradas equilibradas para empresas que produzem, comercializam, empregam e investem no Brasil. articles.title: Senado aprova MP que põe fim à taxa das blusinhas
articles.titleKo: Senado aprova MP que põe fim à taxa das blusinhas
articles.originalSummary: O Plenário do Senado aprovou nesta quinta-feira, 3, a medida provisória que põe fim à chamada taxa das blusinhas. A MP 1.357/2026 zera o Imposto de Importação sobre compras internacionais de até US$ 50. A proposta já havia sido aprovada pela comissão mista, na quarta-feira, 2, e pelo Plenário da Câmara, na tarde desta quinta. Agora, segue para sanção presidencial. As compras internacionais continuam sujeitas ao Imposto sobre Circulação de Mercadorias e Serviços (ICMS), com alíquotas definidas pelos estados e pelo Distrito Federal. A relatora da proposta na comissão mista, senadora Leila Barros (PDT-DF), afirmou que a redução do Imposto de Importação para compras de pequeno valor representa uma medida de justiça tributária para consumidores de menor renda. Além da desoneração, o texto estabelece regras para fiscalização e transparência das plataformas de comércio eletrônico, combate a fraudes e avaliação periódica dos efeitos da medida sobre a economia brasileira. Entre as mudanças estão a adoção de medidas contra a venda de produtos ilegais, a possibilidade de estabelecer limites de quantidade ou frequência para o uso da alíquota reduzida e avaliações periódicas dos impactos da desoneração sobre emprego, indústria, comércio, preços e arrecadação. O texto também autoriza o Ministério da Fazenda a modificar as alíquotas do Imposto de Importação no Regime de Tributação Simplificada (RTS). A alíquota poderá ser reduzida a zero para compras de até US$ 50 e a 30% para remessas de até US$ 3 mil. A legislação anterior estabelecia alíquota mínima de 20% para remessas de até US$ 50 e de até 60% para compras de até US$ 3 mil, além do ICMS. O Ministério da Fazenda poderá ainda estabelecer alíquotas diferentes conforme a modalidade de transporte da encomenda e a adesão da plataforma ao programa de conformidade da Receita Federal. Medicamentos Entre as emendas acolhidas está a que zera o Imposto de Importação sobre medicamentos sem similar nacional adquiridos por pessoas físicas para uso próprio no tratamento de doenças raras ou negligenciadas. Impacto econômico O texto determina que o Ministério da Fazenda avalie periodicamente os efeitos econômicos da tributação das remessas internacionais. O primeiro levantamento deverá ser concluído e publicado em até três meses, e os seguintes deverão ser realizados em intervalos de, no máximo, seis meses. A análise deverá considerar impactos sobre emprego e renda, competitividade da indústria e do varejo, preços de produtos de consumo popular, volume e origem das remessas, diferenças tributárias entre produtos importados e nacionais e efeitos sobre a arrecadação. O acompanhamento deverá abranger os setores têxtil, de vestuário, calçados, acessórios, brinquedos e cosméticos. Responsabilização das plataformas O texto também amplia a responsabilidade das plataformas de comércio eletrônico e dos operadores logísticos. As empresas habilitadas no programa de conformidade deverão adotar mecanismos para identificar indícios de subfaturamento, fracionamento artificial de encomendas e ocultação do remetente. As plataformas também deverão verificar dados cadastrais dos vendedores, oferecer canais para denúncias de produtos ilegais ou que violem direitos de propriedade intelectual e retirar ofertas irregulares. O descumprimento das regras poderá resultar em advertência, multa, suspensão temporária e, em casos mais graves ou reiterados, proibição de operar no mercado brasileiro. articles.title: CEO da Chilli Beans diz estar em negociações com parceiros após notícia sobre recuperação judicial
articles.titleKo: CEO da Chilli Beans diz estar em negociações com parceiros após notícia sobre recuperação judicial
articles.originalSummary: A Chilli Beans está avançando nas negociações com parceiros e trabalhando para fortalecer sua estrutura financeira. A declaração foi feita pelo fundador e CEO da companhia, Caito Maia, em vídeo divulgado nas redes sociais após notícias sobre a situação financeira da empresa, que estaria supostamente analisando um pedido de recuperação judicial . Segundo Maia, a companhia trouxe André Dela Togna e sua equipe para reforçar a estrutura e tornar a área financeira mais sólida. O executivo também afirmou que permanecerá como CEO da empresa, enquanto Togna ocupará o cargo de vice-presidente da marca. “Trouxemos um time para solidificar a estrutura, para deixar o financeiro sólido, porque a gente precisa cada vez mais ter uma base sólida para continuar crescendo”, afirmou. Na mensagem, Maia disse ainda que a empresa cresceu 10% em agosto, no período do Dia dos Pais, e destacou os planos da marca para o próximo ano, quando a Chilli Beans completa 30 anos. articles.title: MP da “taxa das blusinhas” é aprovada na Câmara e vai ao Senado
articles.titleKo: MP da “taxa das blusinhas” é aprovada na Câmara e vai ao Senado
articles.originalSummary: O plenário da Câmara dos Deputados aprovou, nesta quinta-feira, 3, em votação simbólica, a Medida Provisória (MP) da chamada “taxa das blusinhas”. O texto zera o imposto de 20% sobre compras internacionais até 50 dólares (cerca de R$ 257) feitas pela internet por meio de remessas postais. Agora, o texto segue para votação no Senado . Segundo o presidente da Câmara, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), as compras de até 50 dólares representam alternativa importante de consumo, especialmente para a população de menor renda. “São brasileiros que enfrentam diariamente a pressão sobre o orçamento doméstico e encontram nesse comércio uma forma de adquirir produtos do cotidiano a preços mais acessíveis”, destacou o parlamentar ao final da votação. De acordo com Motta, as preocupações da indústria e do varejo nacionais, setores que são contrários ao fim da taxa, serão debatidas para conciliar a proteção do poder de compra das famílias e manter a competitividade da produção brasileira. A MP precisa ser aprovada nas duas Casas do Legislativo, até 8 de setembro, para não perder a validade. Alterações no texto Durante a tramitação, o texto foi modificado pela relatora na comissão especial mista, a senadora Leila Barros (PDT-DF). Uma das novidades introduzidas na medida é a emenda que zera o imposto de importação de medicamentos que não tem versão similar no Brasil. A MP aprovada também prevê uma redução de 60% para 30% da alíquota de importação para compras de até US$ 3 mil por remessas postais vindas do exterior. Outro ponto incluído é a previsão de avaliação periódica, pelo Ministério da Fazenda, dos efeitos econômicos da isenção tarifária. Parlamentares da oposição criticaram o teor da medida por dar vantagem a empresas estrangeiras em detrimento da indústria nacional. “O exato benefício fiscal que está sendo dado para o mesmíssimo produto com o mesmíssimo preço precisa ser dado para o brasileiro, para quem produz aqui, para quem ainda acredita no Brasil”, afirmou o deputado federal Gilson Marques (Novo-SC). articles.title: Uber anuncia corte de cerca de 10% de sua força de trabalho global
articles.titleKo: Uber anuncia corte de cerca de 10% de sua força de trabalho global
articles.originalSummary: A Uber anunciou uma reestruturação global que resultará na redução de cerca de 10% de sua força de trabalho. A decisão foi comunicada pelo CEO da companhia, Dara Khosrowshahi, em uma carta enviada aos colaboradores. Segundo o executivo, os funcionários afetados pelas demissões já foram notificados, com exceção dos países em que ainda são necessários procedimentos locais. A reestruturação prevê a redução de níveis hierárquicos, a simplificação das equipes e mudanças na estratégia de localização dos funcionários. De acordo com Khosrowshahi, o objetivo é tornar a organização mais enxuta e direcionar recursos para áreas consideradas prioritárias pela empresa. “Essas mudanças dizem respeito à nossa organização e às nossas prioridades, e não às contribuições individuais”, afirmou o CEO na carta. A Uber também planeja concentrar suas equipes em um número menor de polos. Os principais times globais ficarão concentrados, principalmente, em Nova York e São Francisco, enquanto a companhia pretende reduzir o trabalho remoto. Segundo a empresa, apenas cerca de 1% dos funcionários deverá continuar trabalhando remotamente. A companhia afirmou que pretende reinvestir as economias geradas pela reestruturação em crescimento, inovação e áreas estratégicas para os próximos anos. articles.title: Nike, Adidas e Asics oferecem descontos sobre descontos na rede Outlet Premium
articles.titleKo: Nike, Adidas e Asics oferecem descontos sobre descontos na rede Outlet Premium
articles.originalSummary: A General Shopping e Outlets do Brasil anuncia a realização da segunda edição da campanha Etiqueta Dourada em toda a rede Outlet Premium, nos dias 11, 12 e 13 de setembro, com a participação de marcas como Nike, Adidas, Asics , Boss, Lacoste e Fila, que oferecerão descontos sobre descontos. Os empreendimentos participantes são: Outlet Premium São Paulo (Itupeva, SP); Outlet Premium Grande São Paulo (Itaquaquecetuba, SP); Outlet Premium Imigrantes (São Bernardo do Campo, SP); Outlet Premium Rio de Janeiro (Duque de Caxias, RJ); Outlet Premium Brasília (Alexânia, GO); Outlet Premium Salvador (Camaçari, BA); Outlet Premium Fortaleza (Caucaia, CE). O horário de funcionamento será das 9h às 21h. “A segunda edição da Etiqueta Dourada marca a consolidação de uma campanha que já se destacou em nossa rede. Unimos uma excelente curadoria de marcas desejadas a um ambiente de compras extremamente agradável e a céu aberto. Desenvolvemos experiências que dialogam com o perfil de cada praça, garantindo que a visita ao Outlet Premium seja sempre um programa inesquecível para toda a família”, afirma a head de Marketing da General Shopping e Outlets do Brasil, Diedre Curalov. A ação foi posicionada na semana do Dia do Cliente, celebrado em 15 de setembro. Durante os três dias, além dos descontos em marcas nacionais e internacionais, o público terá acesso a opções de lazer. Durante o fim de semana da Etiqueta Dourada, o público contará com apresentações de música ao vivo, espaços de diversão infantil, atrações artísticas e ativações que variam conforme o calendário de cada unidade. Para os consumidores que desejam planejar as compras com antecedência, os outlets disponibilizarão uma curadoria de ofertas em suas vitrines virtuais, além de transmissões ao vivo nas redes sociais com os principais produtos da campanha. articles.title: Rosati’s Pizza Plans 11 Openings Over 90 Days
articles.titleKo: Rosati’s Pizza Plans 11 Openings Over 90 Days
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Rosati’s Pizza Enterprises, Inc., the franchisor behind the iconic Chicago-style pizza brand, Rosati’s Pizza, today announced an unprecedented period of development momentum marked by the planned opening of 11 new locations over the next 90 days. This rapid store expansion propels the company to two record-breaking milestones in the brands 62-year history: achieving the highest number of new store openings in a single year and reaching the largest percentage of multi-unit operators within its national franchise network since the brand’s founding in 1964. “Opening 11 new stores in just three months is a testament to the enduring strength of our brand legacy and unit-level economics,” said Anthony Rosati, owner of Rosati’s Pizza Enterprises, Inc. “Achieving record-setting annual store growth and our highest number of multi-unit operators in company history underscores the deep confidence our franchise partners have in Rosati’s long-term business model.” The 90-day expansion spree caps off a historic growth phase for the restaurant franchise. Annually ranked in Entrepreneur magazine’s Franchise 500® and Franchise Times Top 400®, voted back-to-back #1 Best Chicago Pizza, the company’s multi-unit momentum reflects both strong consumer brand affinity and robust systemwide franchise support. The upcoming store launches highlight accelerated demand from both single-unit franchisees and existing multi-unit operators scaling their portfolios into expansion territories nationwide. Streamlined commercial real estate site selection, flexible retail footprint options (including end caps and second-generation restaurant conversions, turnkey construction workflows, and dedicated field operations support have enabled local franchise owners to bring units from lease signing to grand opening efficiently. With development momentum at an all-time high, Rosati’s Pizza Enterprises continues to partner with multi-unit restaurant groups, experienced multi-unit brand operators, and franchise brokers to identify qualified candidates and secure prime commercial real estate markets. Segafredo, a global authority in authentic Italian espresso and part of the Massimo Zanetti Beverage USA (MZB-USA) portfolio, announced the official launch of Segafredo Cold Espresso on September 1. Arriving ahead of high-volume autumn and holiday seasons, this new product gives restaurant operators, beverage directors, mixologists, and culinary teams an immediate, profitable solution to the operational bottlenecks of espresso drinks. As espresso beverages continue their rapid rise—led by the Espresso Martini boasting a +213% four-year menu growth and holding the No. 1 spot as the most-ordered cocktail in fine dining, according to Datasenntial Menu Trends—foodservice programs face unprecedented pressure on speed of service, labor costs, and quality control. Segafredo Cold Espresso addresses these friction points head-on across cocktail, zero-proof, and culinary applications. “For more than 50 years, Segafredo has been defined by uncompromising Italian craftsmanship, but true leadership means evolving alongside the hospitality industry’s changing operational needs,” said Matthew Smith, President of Massimo Zanetti Beverage USA. “With Cold Espresso, we are combining our deep espresso heritage with modern beverage innovation. We’re giving operators a powerful tool that protects their bottom line while driving high-margin menu revenue during the busiest quarter of the year.” Real Espresso, Zero Operational Headache Segafredo Cold Espresso is not a concentrate or cold brew. It is 100% authentic espresso cold-extracted to preserve the bold, smooth taste profile of traditional Segafredo espresso. Without the need for commercial machinery or hours of pre-shift prep, operators can execute flawless espresso martinis, zero-proof mocktails, affogatos, and modern beverage builds in seconds. “Segafredo Cold Espresso was crafted as a premium, high-performance ingredient that expands what’s possible across the modern menu,” said Erica Beilenson, SVP of Marketing at MZB-USA. “Demand for real, high-quality espresso flavor has never been higher, and today’s culinary and beverage directors need an authentic asset that performs seamlessly everywhere – from craft cocktails and zero-proof offerings to desserts and savory applications. Staff shouldn’t have to battle machine maintenance or pre-chilling shots during a peak dinner push. Cold Espresso sits right in the speed rail or kitchen line, accepts standard pourers, and delivers a rich, natural crema every single time.” Key Product Specifications & F&B Benefits Built for Fast Workflows: Packaged in a 24 fl oz bottle designed specifically to fit standard speed rails and accept universal speed pourers. articles.title: Hai Hospitality Names Carl Segal First COO
articles.titleKo: Hai Hospitality Names Carl Segal First COO
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Hai Hospitality, the James Beard Foundation Award-winning Austin-based restaurant group behind Uchi, Uchiko, Uchibā, Loro Asian Smokehouse & Bar and Oheya, has appointed Carl Segal as its first Chief Operating Officer. Segal officially joined the company on August 24 and will oversee restaurant operations across Hai Hospitality’s growing portfolio. Segal brings decades of experience spanning restaurant operations, entrepreneurship and executive leadership within emerging and established multi-unit hospitality organizations. He began his career with Lettuce Entertain You in Chicago before becoming a restaurant owner himself. Segal later spent thirteen years with Potbelly Sandwich Works, helping grow the company from a single Chicago restaurant to nearly 300 locations domestically and internationally. He was also part of the leadership team that took Potbelly public in 2013. Segal went on to serve as CEO of Roti Modern Mediterranean, where he helped grow and reposition the brand, and held senior leadership roles at REEF Technology. Most recently, he served as Chief Operating Officer of José Andrés Group, leading operations across its multi-concept hospitality organization. “Carl brings the depth of operating experience we need as Hai enters its next stage of growth, but what stood out most was how closely his leadership philosophy aligns with our culture,” said Tony Montero, Chief Executive Officer of Hai Hospitality. “He understands that great hospitality begins with great people. His commitment to supporting restaurant teams, protecting what makes each concept special and building for sustainable growth makes him an ideal fit for Hai.” As Chief Operating Officer, Segal will work closely with Hai’s leadership and operations teams to strengthen restaurant performance, support the employee and guest experience, and help guide the company’s continued expansion. “Hai has built an extraordinary collection of restaurants by pairing a relentless commitment to quality with a culture that values creativity and invests in its people,” said Segal. “I’m excited to spend time with the teams, learn what makes these restaurants so special and help build the operational foundation that will support Hai’s future while preserving the qualities that have made the company successful.” Segal is a graduate of the University of Wisconsin and has completed executive education at Harvard Business School. articles.title: PAR Technology Launches Guest360 to Unify Restaurant Guest Data
articles.titleKo: PAR Technology Launches Guest360 to Unify Restaurant Guest Data
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . PAR Technology Corporation announced the launch of Guest360, a new product designed to help restaurant brands understand and grow their entire guest base, not just the guests enrolled in loyalty. Built to work alongside PAR Punchh, Guest360 recognizes guests from the first transaction, connects their activity across channels, and creates unified profiles that enable more powerful guest engagement and experiences for brands. Guest360 is already live with select Punchh customers, with rollout expanding to all Punchh customers through the end of 2026. Guest360 builds on the foundation PAR established with Punchh, which helps over 200 enterprise brands understand and grow their loyalty members. Most restaurant transactions happen outside the loyalty program, across POS, kiosk, drive-thru, pay-at-table, ordering, and delivery, leaving brands with guest activity that is often anonymous, duplicated, or disconnected. Guest360 closes that gap by recognizing guests from the moment they transact, connecting their behavior across channels, and making that understanding immediately available for segmentation, personalization, and activation. “Most restaurants know their loyalty members well, but that’s only a fraction of their guests,” said Savneet Singh, CEO of PAR Technology. “Guest360 is a customer data platform, natively integrated into the PAR Punchh suite, that unifies every guest interaction into a single profile. Every transaction builds a profile, every profile builds understanding, and that understanding compounds over time into something no generic AI tool can replicate. Because Guest360 is built into Punchh, it works with the data brands already have. This is what it looks like when first- and third-party data actually works for the brand.” At the core of Guest360 is Profile Stitching, technology that consolidates a guest’s activity across channels, whether at the drive-thru, on a kiosk, or through the mobile app, into a single, lasting profile rather than fragmented or duplicate records. That unified view also powers PAR Intelligence, which recommends the next audience, campaign, or move based on what Guest360 surfaces, growing sharper with every additional data source a brand connects. Guest360 was built in close partnership with Punchh customers and its product advisory group, whose input shaped how the product recognizes, segments, and activates guests for multi-unit operations. Because Guest360 is connected directly to Punchh, the audiences it uncovers do not need to be exported into another marketing platform before a brand can act. Restaurants can automatically trigger personalized offers, win-back journeys, loyalty enrollment campaigns, and other experiences based on real guest behavior, then tie the resulting visit and spend back to POS revenue. Here’s what brands can expect from Guest360: • Guest Recognition: Recognizes guests from POS, ordering, and payment activity, connecting transactions and accounts into one profile per guest. • Unified Guest Profiles: Builds a single profile per guest from in-store behavior, digital activity, and loyalty data, enriched with visit patterns, purchases, and lifecycle stage. • Behavioral Segmentation: Creates dynamic audiences that update automatically based on real spend, visit frequency, menu preference, and lifecycle stage across loyalty and non-loyalty guests. • Activation: Turns guest behavior into action directly within Punchh, from personalized offers and win-back journeys to loyalty conversion and milestone campaigns, without moving audiences into another platform. • Closed-Loop Measurement: Connects campaigns back to POS transactions and item-level revenue so brands can measure what actually drove a visit or sale. Zaxbys, the fast-casual restaurant known for its signature Chicken Fingerz, Zax Sauce and Southern hospitality, is officially coming to West Tennessee with a new location opening at 1328 Mineral Wells Ave. in Paris on Tuesday, Sept. 8. The restaurant marks the first Zaxbys in Henry County and the brand’s 13 th in Tennessee. The grand opening celebration will invite local residents and community members to experience the brand, meet the team and be among the first to enjoy the craveable menu. “Paris is exactly the kind of community we’re excited to be a part of,” said Drew Gressett, CEO of Roost & Rise Holdings. “We know what makes Zaxbys special goes beyond the amazing food. We’re excited to bring that experience to Henry County and become part of the community.” The Paris location will serve Zaxbys fresh, prepared-to-order Chicken Fingerz and wings tossed in a variety of bold and spicy sauces, along with its popular Chicken Bacon Ranch Loaded Fries and fan-favorite Fried Pickles. The menu also features Wings & Things, Big Zax Snak, Zalads and sandwiches, served with crinkle-cut fries, Texas Toast and the brand’s iconic Zax Sauce. From quick lunches to family dinners, guests can expect the signature flavors and generous portions that have made the brand a favorite across the Southeast. The opening supports the continued growth of Roost & Rise Holdings, one of Zaxbys largest franchise operators, and expands the brand’s footprint across Tennessee while bringing its signature experience to more guests. “We are extremely happy to welcome Zaxbys to our community,” said Caleb Grissom, executive director at Paris-Henry County Chamber of Commerce. “The opening of Zaxby’s represents more than the addition of a new restaurant. This is truly a shift forward for the future of Paris and Henry County. New businesses create jobs, strengthen our local economy and enhance the quality of life for those who call our community home.” Zaxbys Paris will be open Sunday through Thursday from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. and Friday and Saturday from 10 a.m. to 11 p.m. For more information about Zaxbys, visit zaxbys.com. Groups interested in hosting a September fundraiser can submit a request at www.blazepizza.com/fundraising. Once the form is completed, the request is routed directly to the local Blaze Pizza restaurant for review and event setup. articles.title: Caribou Coffee Names Zane Thomas-Rogers COO
articles.titleKo: Caribou Coffee Names Zane Thomas-Rogers COO
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Zane Thomas-Rogers brings more than 15 years’ experience leading large, complex operations for major, company-owned and franchised restaurant brands. Caribou Coffee, the national operator of premium coffeehouses, announced today the appointment of Zane Thomas-Rogers as Chief Operations Officer. The role will bring a greater focus on coffeehouse operations and excellence as warehouse management and logistics now fall under the supervision of Caribou’s supply chain team. The move follows senior leadership additions over the past year in finance, marketing, real estate development, supply chain and technology, as well as the company’s first Chief Commercial Officer, Matt Reiter. Thomas-Rogers joins Caribou Coffee with a strong background in leading large, complex, multi-unit restaurant operations. He was most recently with Raising Cane’s and steps into the Chief Operating Officer role being vacated by John Walbrun. Walbrun announced his retirement recently, after more than eight years – a period that saw the company expand coffeehouse operations in the U.S., particularly in southeastern states, as well as the opening of a new, larger warehouse facility. Walbrun will stay at Caribou in a strategic advisor role for the next few months to help with the transition. “We are evolving the Caribou organization to be flatter, with leaders who bring true subject matter expertise and are very hands-on with their teams” said Scott Kennedy, CEO, Caribou Coffee. “As part of our plan to deliver a consistent exceptional guest experience, maintain product excellence, and to grow our business in a smart, measured way, we’ve sharpened the way we think about our Chief Operations Officer role. Zane will bring an enhanced, field-centric approach, utilizing his proven operational expertise and leadership, to ensure the strategic decisions we make at our Support Center positively impact and improve what we do in every coffeehouse and cup we serve. He also has a reputation as a steady, team-first and collaborative leader – all qualities that fit perfectly with our culture and how we run our business.” Thomas-Rogers brings more than 15 years’ experience leading large, complex operations for major, company-owned and franchised restaurant brands. He has a successful track record of developing high-performing, supportive teams and bringing a data-led approach to operational decision-making — both critical as Caribou continues to invest in elevating the guest experience and technology that improves efficiency across the business. “I could feel the momentum at Caribou from my earliest meetings with Scott and his team,” said Zane Thomas-Rogers, Chief Operations Officer. “But then, attending our annual conference, BouCon, to hear the strategic plans already underway and spending a few weeks in coffeehouses with our managers and teams, I saw a companywide energy as we double down on exceptional guest experience and product quality. So, it’s a really exciting time to be taking the operational reigns.” For more information visit www.cariboucoffee.com. KFC Global announced that Amy Ellis Durini will join KFC as Global Chief Brand Officer (CBO), reporting directly to Scott Mezvinsky, KFC Global Chief Executive Officer (CEO), effective November 1, 2026. In the newly created role, Amy will lead KFC’s global brand strategy, overseeing brand, loyalty and retail, as well as new concept development and innovation – creating relevant and distinctive ways for KFC to engage with today’s consumers. Amy will also partner closely with KFC’s CMO community across markets, working closely with marketing leaders to continue modernizing the KFC expression and experience around the world. Amy joins KFC from Taco Bell International, where she most recently served as Chief Marketing and Strategy Officer. In that role, Amy worked closely with markets to bring the magic of Taco Bell to consumers around the world, shaping how the brand showed up across marketing, digital, value and the broader consumer experience. She also helped bring to life some of Taco Bell International’s largest campaigns and cultural moments, including Encore Hours, Crossbar Bong, Live Mas Club, while expanding Taco Con to bring franchise partners, marketers and Taco Bell teams together from around the world to share and learn from one another. Before joining Taco Bell in 2021, Amy spent eight years across KFC Global and Latin America & Caribbean. articles.titleKo: Chicken Salad Chick Opens in Barboursville, West Virginia
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Chicken Salad Chick, the nation’s only fast casual chicken salad restaurant concept, announced today the opening of its first restaurant in The Mountain State, which will expand the brand’s footprint to 26 states. The new restaurant is located at 21 Tanyard Station Drive in the Tanyard Station shopping center in Barboursville. The community is invited to celebrate the grand opening on Wednesday, September 16, when the first 100 guests in line will win free chicken salad for a year*. During the grand opening week, guests can expect to experience the Southern hospitality Chicken Salad Chick is known for while taking advantage of various specials and giveaways. These include: Wednesday, September 16 – Free Chicken Salad for a Year to the First 100 Guests – The first guest in line at 10am will receive one FREE large Quick Chick of chicken salad per week for an entire year. The next 99 guests in line will receive one FREE large Quick Chick of chicken salad per month for a year. Thursday, September 17 – The first 50 guests at 10am and 5pm to purchase a meal with two sides or equivalent will receive a FREE Chick Tote Bag!** Friday, September 18 – The first 50 guests at 10am and 5pm to purchase a meal with two sides or equivalent will receive a FREE Chick Tumbler!** Saturday, September 19 – The first 50 guests at 10am and 5pm to purchase two large Quick Chicks or equivalent will receive a FREE Red Grocery Tote!*** Sunday, September 20 – The first 50 guests at 10am and 5pm to purchase a meal with one side will receive a FREE Meal with One Side on your next visit!**** Chicken Salad Chick of Barboursville is owned and operated by first-time franchise owners and couple, Tammy and Rancie Hannah. Prior to franchising, Tammy spent over 30 years in pharmaceutical sales at Pfizer, and Rancie is a practicing physician in Russell, Kentucky where he provides hospice care. They both built careers around serving others with compassion and hospitality and believe these skills will transfer well to franchise ownership. Their son, who is graduating with a bachelor’s degree in business from Eastern Kentucky University this May, may also join the family business and assist with operations following graduation. Beyond their professional lives, the Hannahs are active members of Greenup Christian Church and view community service as an important part of their fellowship. They have been loyal Chicken Salad Chick customers for years and had always been interested in opening a restaurant of their own. When they learned about an opportunity to bring the brand to Ashland, Kentucky, they jumped at the chance and also agreed to open the franchise’s first West Virigina restaurant. “I’m so excited to bring Chicken Salad Chick to West Virginia for the first time and expand soon in the tri-state area,” said Tammy Hannah, franchise owner of Chicken Salad Chick of Barboursville. “What I’m most looking forward to, besides meeting our customers, is building meaningful community connections and creating a welcoming space where our guests feel right at home. articles.title: Chicken Salad Chick Unveils Spicy New Nashville Hottie and Pumpkin Spice Cake for Fall
articles.titleKo: Chicken Salad Chick Unveils Spicy New Nashville Hottie and Pumpkin Spice Cake for Fall
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Chicken Salad Chick, the nation’s only fast casual chicken salad restaurant concept, announced the arrival of two new limited-time menu items and two returning favorites to bring together the best of fall flavor. Launching August 31, guests can enjoy the debut of Nashville Hottie chicken salad and Pumpkin Spice Cake, alongside the return of Chicken Poblano Soup and Lemon Burst Buttercream Cookies as part ofthe brand’s annual fundraising campaign supporting CURE Childhood Cancer. As the weather begins to cool, Chicken Salad Chick is turning up the heat with the launch of the all-new Nashville Hottie, the brand’s hottest flavor yet. Inspired by the bold flavors of Nashville hot chicken, Nashville Hottie combines fiery Nashville-style heat with tangy dill pickle pieces. Guests can enjoy Nashville Hottie as a scoop, sandwich, melt or Quick Chick, and it can also be ordered as a featured flavor for catering orders. Guests can also pair Nashville Hottie with one of Chicken Salad Chick’s fan-favorite seasonal soups: the Chicken Poblano Soup. The flavor is returning to Chicken Salad Chick’s soup schedule and will be served daily throughout the fall. Featuring a creamy blend of diced chicken, poblano peppers, corn, black beans and a hint of lime, the hearty soup makes the perfect companion to Nashville Hottie’s flavorful kick. For guests who can’t get enough of pumpkin spice season, Chicken Salad Chick is also introducing a brand-new dessert – Pumpkin Spice Cake. This decadent fall staple is a triple-layer pumpkin spice cake wrapped in velvety cream cheese frosting, delivering the perfect balance of warm fall spices and creamy sweetness. Available by the slice in restaurant and online, the Pumpkin Spice Cake can also be ordered whole through catering. The limited-time dessert marks Chicken Salad Chick’s third cake flavor launch, following the success of White Chocolate Cake and Red Velvet Cake. “Our guests tell us what they want, and lately that’s bold, on-trend flavors they can only find here,” said Scott Deviney, President and CEO of Chicken Salad Chick. “We’ve put a lot of work into our menu innovation pipeline so we can keep bringing them something new each season without losing the classics they count on. Nashville Hottie and the Pumpkin Spice Cake are a fun take on fall, whether you’re craving something spicy, sweet or a little bit of both.” In addition to these new flavors, Chicken Salad Chick will once again be supporting CURE Childhood Cancer , an Atlanta-based nonprofit dedicated to funding life-changing pediatric cancer research and supporting children and families nationwide, through its annual Cookies for a CURE fundraising campaign all September long. Now in its fifth consecutive year, a portion of proceeds from each Lemon Burst Buttercream Cookie sold during Childhood Cancer Awareness Month will help fund critical research and patient support programs. The Lemon Burst Buttercream Cookie, a sweet tribute to the gold ribbon that symbolizes childhood cancer awareness, is topped with a natural lemon zest buttercream frosting. It’s available for purchase in-restaurant or online. Since 2017, the Chicken Salad Chick Foundation has donated more than $2 million to support pediatric cancer research and fight food insecurity in local communities. During Chicken Salad Chick’s annual owner conference in March, the brand presented CURE Childhood Cancer with a record-breaking donation of $382,604.30, representing funds raised through the 2025 CURE campaign and year-end Giving Card program. The donation surpassed the previous year’s total by more than $50,000, marking the largest single contribution in the partnership’s history. articles.title: Krystal Launches New Hasbro-Powered Kids Meals and 99-Cent Sunday Deal for Families

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Krystal is introducing new Kids Meals featuring collectible toys from Hasbro, a leading games, IP and toy company, alongside a limited-time 99-cent Kids Meal offer on Sundays in participating markets as families settle back into school-year routines. Together, the offerings make Krystal one of the most affordable family dining options among quick-service restaurants. The new Kids Meals feature collectible toys from two of Hasbro’s popular franchises, My Little Pony and Tonka . The toys give kids something fun to collect while tapping into nostalgia for many parents. “Families are making real trade-offs right now, and they’re paying attention to where their money goes,” said Kaitlin Kees, Senior Director of Marketing at Krystal. “A Kids Meal with a toy children recognize, at a price parents can feel good about, is exactly the kind of value families are looking for this time of year.” Each Kids Meal includes a choice of entrée — a Krystal Slider, Cheese Krystal, Classic Pup, Corn Pup or four-piece all-white-meat Chicken Nuggets — along with small fries or tots, a drink (milk, lemonade or bottled water), an activity sheet, crayons, a Hasbro-branded cup and a collectible toy. For guests new to the brand, the signature Krystal slider features a thin, square 100% USDA beef patty steamed on a bed of diced onions and served with yellow mustard, dill pickle and a soft steamed bun. It’s been prepared the same way since 1932. For a limited time in participating markets, Kids Meals will be available for just 99 cents on Sundays, making Krystal one of the few quick-service restaurant brands offering a Kids Meal for less than a dollar. Available now through Nov. 1, the promotion spans the back-to-school season and continues through the fall. Guests can also join Club Krystal through the Krystal app to order ahead, access delivery, earn rewards and receive additional app-exclusive offers throughout the promotion. Two Los Angeles favorites are rolling up something unexpected this September. All About the Cinnamon and Prince St. Pizza are teaming up to launch “The Prince”, a limited-edition savory pizza bun combining All About the Cinnamon’s signature handcrafted dough with the iconic marinara and famed crispy, cupped-and-charred pepperoni cups of Prince St. Pizza. Available September 4 through September 27, The Prince takes the soft, freshly baked dough behind All About the Cinnamon’s signature rolls and gives it a savory spin, layering in Prince St. Pizza’s signature pizza sauce and fresh mozzarella for a mashup that lands somewhere between a freshly baked roll and a slice of pizza. The Prince will be available in two varieties: Cheese for $11 and Pepperoni for $12, with Prince St. Pizza’s Not Ranch available for an additional $2.50. Each roll will be made fresh in limited quantities daily with a side of Prince St. Pizza’s housemade marinara sauce. The Prince will be available while supplies last. “We’ve always loved taking something familiar and finding a way to make it completely our own and The Prince was such a fun opportunity to step outside of what people normally expect from us,” said Lindsay Sears-McDonald, owner of All About the Cinnamon. “Prince St. Pizza has such an iconic flavor and identity, and bringing that together with our dough felt like the perfect collaboration. It’s still unmistakably us, just savory, and we can’t wait for people to try it.” Founded as a family-owned bakery, All About the Cinnamon has built a following around its handcrafted, small-batch cinnamon rolls, combining quality ingredients with a deep love of hip-hop culture. The collaboration marks a playful departure from the bakery’s typically sweet creations while staying true to its approach of using its signature dough as a canvas for bold flavors. “At Prince St. Pizza, we’re always excited by collaborations that feel authentic to both brands rather than simply putting two names together,” said Lawrence Longo, owner of Prince St. Pizza. “All About the Cinnamon has created something really special with their dough, and The Prince brings the best parts of both brands into one bite. It’s fun, unexpected and still has the flavors people immediately recognize as Prince St.” Prince St. Pizza brought its iconic New York slices to Los Angeles in 2019, quickly building a following for its signature Sicilian squares and legendary Spicy Spring. Its Studio City location has become a neighborhood favorite, bringing Prince St.’s downtown New York roots to the Valley while embracing the local community through collaborations, events and partnerships. Throughout the four-week limited time collaboration, The Prince will be available at All About the Cinnamon in Sherman Oaks Wednesday – Sunday at 11 A.M. until sold out, as well as for a limited time on Sundays at Prince St.’s booth in the Studio City Farmers Market. Quantities will be limited, with fresh batches prepared throughout the campaign. articles.title: South Korean Concept Kodachaya Opens in NYC’s Koreatown
articles.titleKo: South Korean Concept Kodachaya Opens in NYC’s Koreatown
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Kodachaya, the Seoul-born dining concept known for its Korean pocha-inspired food, drinks, and nightlife experience, made its New York debut in Manhattan’s Koreatown on July 31. Introduced by Group KFF, the large-scale venue spans 32nd to 33rd Streets near Penn Station, with entrances on both sides of the block and the Empire State Building visible just outside the 33rd Street entrance. Inspired by Korea’s market alleys, pojangmacha, and street food stalls, Kodachaya brings Korean food, drinks, social dining, and entertainment together in one destination. The restaurant is designed like a small Korean market village, with house-like structures, alley-style pathways, wall details, and five food stations offering Korean dishes and pocha-style menus. A 100% open island kitchen allows guests to see the cooking process up close, adding energy and movement to the space. The open layout, market-inspired design, and retro Seoul atmosphere create a dining experience that feels casual, lively, and rooted in Korean food culture. One of Kodachaya’s biggest differences is its no-tipping service model. Guests order and pay through kiosks or QR codes, while staff bring food to the table. Drinks are available through a self-select beverage station, where guests can choose their own beverages, place them in a basket, and pay directly at the station. The system keeps the experience efficient and approachable while helping maintain quality and value across food and drinks. Signature dishes include Kimchi Fried Rice, Italian-Style Sujebi, and Tomato Mussel Jjamppong. Kodachaya’s Kimchi Fried Rice, known as “Kimbbok,” began as a staff meal at the original Garosu-gil location and has since sold more than 2.5 million servings in Korea. Served on a hot iron plate with cheese and a sunny-side-up egg, the dish reflects the brand’s focus on familiar Korean flavors, creative comfort food, and shareable dining. Beyond food and drinks, Kodachaya NYC is built as a social destination. The space includes a Korean-style photo booth for guests to capture moments from their visit, as well as a karaoke space downstairs for those continuing the night after dinner. Open until 4 a.m. on Fridays and Saturdays, Kodachaya offers a new late-night dining and entertainment option in Koreatown. With five kitchens, open cooking stations, no-tipping service, a self-select beverage station, photo moments, karaoke, and retro Seoul energy, Kodachaya brings its signature concept to life in New York. articles.title: Vicious Biscuit Signs Lease in Northeast Ohio
articles.titleKo: Vicious Biscuit Signs Lease in Northeast Ohio
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Vicious Biscuit, the original home of unapologetically bold biscuits, is expanding its footprint in Northeast Ohio as franchisees Carl Albright, Dave Ost and Ken Troutman sign a lease for their third location. The group’s next restaurant is planned for early 2027 at 4693 Fulton Drive NW in Belden Center in Canton, OH. The 5,025-square-foot end-cap space will include a large outdoor patio and marks the halfway point in the group’s six-unit development commitment with Vicious Biscuit. Albright and his partners were the first Vicious Biscuit franchisees to open a restaurant, introducing the concept to Ohio with Montrose in May 2024. They recently became the first franchise group in the system to open a second location with the debut of Medina in June and are now the first to move forward with a third. “Carl and his partners continuing to grow with us is exactly what we want to see as we build this franchise system,” said George McLaughlin, co-founder and CEO of Vicious Biscuit. “They believed in Vicious Biscuit from the beginning, opened our first franchise location and have continued to invest in what we’re building together. When an existing franchisee wants to expand their footprint, that says a lot about their confidence in the concept and where we’re headed.” Medina also marked another milestone for Vicious Biscuit as its first freestanding franchise restaurant. The company currently operates two freestanding corporate locations and sees the format as an important part of its future development strategy as the right real estate becomes available. Medina also gave Vicious Biscuit its first opportunity to apply its market-density strategy outside its home market of Charleston, SC. While Medina and Montrose are geographically close, highways and green space create natural trade-area separation between two communities, supporting the company’s strategy to build greater density in Northeast Ohio. For Vicious Biscuit, that approach is part of a broader development strategy that prioritizes restaurant-level economics and the ideal real estate over opening locations simply to increase unit count. “We’re not interested in growing just to put another number on the board,” McLaughlin said. “The real estate must make sense for the franchisee and give that restaurant the best opportunity to perform for the long term. Sometimes that means being patient and waiting for that opportunity. If we want franchisees to continue growing with us, it’s imperative we make good decisions with their investment.” That next opportunity is in Canton. The new restaurant will be in the Belden Village area near Jackson Township and the Pro Football Hall of Fame, with a mix of established retail, restaurants and residential communities surrounding the site. “As we’ve grown from one location to two and now prepare for our third, we’ve seen the infrastructure Vicious Biscuit has put in place to support franchisees as they grow,” Albright said. “There’s a system behind each new restaurant, from training and operations to support from the corporate team. Knowing that support is there gives us confidence as we continue building our business and moving toward our six-location commitment.” Vicious Biscuit is seeking multi-unit operators to join its growing franchise system. For more information, visit www.viciousbiscuit.com/vicious-biscuit-franchise. The post Vicious Biscuit Signs Lease in Northeast Ohio appeared first on QSR Magazine .
