articles.title: Aos 30 anos, Cia. Tradicional de Comércio leva Bráz a Brasília e avança fora de São Paulo
articles.titleKo: Aos 30 anos, Cia. Tradicional de Comércio leva Bráz a Brasília e avança fora de São Paulo
articles.originalSummary: A Companhia Tradicional de Comércio completa 30 anos ampliando a presença fora do eixo São Paulo. O grupo, responsável por algumas das marcas mais conhecidas da gastronomia paulistana, prepara para até o fim deste ano a abertura de uma Bráz Pizzaria em Brasília, que se somará às operações já existentes no Rio de Janeiro e em Campinas. A nova unidade será uma operação de rua e marcará a estreia da companhia na capital federal. Para João Adas, CEO da Cia. Tradicional de Comércio, Brasília reúne características que justificam o movimento. “Brasília mostra a força da cidade. É uma cidade grande, tem toda a questão do governo que movimenta a cidade durante a semana e tem bons fundamentos”, afirma. A chegada à capital federal ocorre em um momento simbólico. A história do grupo começou com o Original, inaugurado em 29 de agosto de 1996, em Moema, na capital paulista. Cinco amigos identificaram naquele momento uma oportunidade para criar um bar inspirado nos estabelecimentos tradicionais, com chope bem tirado, petiscos e hospitalidade como elementos centrais da experiência. Dois anos depois vieram Pirajá e Bráz. A partir daí, o portfólio foi sendo ampliado com marcas como Astor, Lanchonete da Cidade, Pirajá e outras operações. Diferentemente de grupos que cresceram por aquisições, a Cia. Tradicional desenvolveu internamente suas bandeiras. “Nunca adquirimos nenhuma marca. Todas as marcas foram criadas pelos cinco fundadores ao longo dos anos”, diz Adas. Hoje, a companhia soma 52 unidades, todas próprias. Bráz e Pirajá são as duas marcas que vêm puxando mais fortemente as novas aberturas. Em 2025, o grupo abriu quatro unidades e fechou duas, parte delas em um processo de revisão do modelo da Bráz Elettrica. Segundo Adas, 2025 também foi “o melhor ano da companhia”. No ano passado, mais de 4 milhões de clientes passaram pelos restaurantes do grupo. A companhia não divulga faturamento. Campinas virou laboratório para sair de São Paulo A presença fora da capital paulista ainda é pequena em relação ao tamanho total da operação, mas vem ganhando importância na estratégia. Em Campinas, a companhia possui quatro restaurantes: três unidades do Pirajá e uma da Bráz. Há operações em shopping centers e também em rua. No Rio de Janeiro, a Bráz está presente no Jardim Botânico. “A gente adora Campinas. É perto, tem uma cultura parecida”, afirma Adas. Segundo o executivo, o desempenho na cidade reforçou a capacidade das marcas de funcionar além de seu mercado original. Brasília será o próximo teste. A escolha da Bráz para entrar na cidade também não é casual. Entre as bandeiras do grupo, a pizzaria é hoje aquela com presença geográfica mais diversificada. “Vamos com a Bráz Pizzaria, testando uma cidade nova, além de Rio de Janeiro e Campinas, onde a gente já está”, diz o CEO. Depois de Brasília, outras regiões estão no radar, mas sem uma corrida por pontos. Adas cita Belo Horizonte e, em uma etapa posterior, mercados do Sul, como Curitiba, Porto Alegre e a região de Itajaí. Expansão exige cautela O plano de crescer fora de São Paulo vem acompanhado de uma postura conservadora em relação à velocidade das aberturas. Restaurantes exigem capital antes mesmo de começarem a gerar receita, desde a obra e instalação de equipamentos até a montagem das equipes. Em um ambiente de juros elevados, o custo de errar aumenta. “A gente faz com bastante diligência a expansão. Sabemos o quão dolorosa pode ser uma expansão se eventualmente dá errado, especialmente fora da cidade, fora do nosso olhar”, afirma Adas. O executivo diz que uma nova praça exige presença, conhecimento local e capacidade da estrutura de liderança para acompanhar a operação. Diferentemente de negócios com ativos mais facilmente transferíveis, boa parte do investimento feito em um restaurante fica presa ao ponto escolhido caso a operação não tenha o desempenho esperado. A cautela também reflete a leitura de Adas sobre o atual momento da alimentação fora do lar. Embora veja fundamentos de longo pr
koreanSummary: A Companhia Tradicional de Comércio completa 30 anos ampliando a presença fora do eixo São Paulo.

articles.title: O que o varejo europeu pode ensinar à moda brasileira?
articles.titleKo: O que o varejo europeu pode ensinar à moda brasileira?
articles.originalSummary: Durante muitos anos, quando o varejo brasileiro queria olhar para o futuro, o destino era quase sempre o mesmo: os Estados Unidos. Nova York se tornou nossa grande vitrine de inovação — e continua sendo uma referência importante. Mas, para quem trabalha com moda , ampliar o repertório geográfico também significa ampliar a capacidade de interpretar diferentes modelos de negócio, comportamentos e relações de consumo. A Europa oferece uma perspectiva diferente. Não necessariamente porque esteja mais avançada em tecnologia ou porque tenha respostas prontas para os desafios do varejo, mas porque reúne, de maneira muito particular, duas forças que a moda conhece bem: tradição e reinvenção. Em Paris, Milão, Londres e outras capitais europeias, convivem marcas centenárias que continuam encontrando novas formas de se relacionar com o consumidor, negócios que questionam modelos tradicionais e lojas que assumem funções que vão muito além da venda. Há uma relação particular com a história, cultura, território e identidade. E isso ganha ainda mais relevância em um momento em que a tecnologia torna produtos, serviços e experiências cada vez mais fáceis de reproduzir. É justamente aí que surge uma provocação importante para a moda brasileira. Enquanto boa parte da discussão sobre o futuro do varejo está concentrada em digitalização, Inteligência Artificial, eficiência operacional e novas experiências, quanto espaço estamos dando àquilo que torna uma marca reconhecível e desejada antes mesmo de a tecnologia entrar em cena? A tecnologia pode melhorar uma operação, acelerar processos, personalizar uma experiência e abrir novas possibilidades de relacionamento, mas não substitui a construção de uma identidade. Uma loja pode ser tecnologicamente sofisticada e não deixar nenhuma lembrança. Uma coleção pode acompanhar perfeitamente as tendências e, ainda assim, não construir uma linguagem própria. Esse talvez seja um dos paradoxos do varejo contemporâneo: quanto mais ferramentas se tornam acessíveis a todos, mais difícil pode ser criar diferenciação a partir delas. Nesse cenário, repertório, identidade, contexto e consistência de marca ganham outro peso. Não como conceitos abstratos, mas como ativos que ajudam a explicar por que determinados negócios conseguem permanecer relevantes enquanto outros, mesmo acompanhando todas as novidades, acabam parecendo iguais. Mas existe uma questão ainda mais importante quando se observa outro mercado: o que estamos vendo é uma tendência ou é a resposta daquele mercado às suas próprias circunstâncias? Uma loja de Paris não opera sob as mesmas regras, custos, fluxos turísticos, regulamentações, hábitos de consumo ou estrutura competitiva de uma loja brasileira. Uma estratégia que parece brilhante em um contexto pode produzir resultados muito diferentes quando transplantada para outro. Por isso, uma boa viagem de pesquisa deveria começar menos pela pergunta “o que podemos copiar?” e mais por “por que isso funciona aqui?” Essa diferença muda completamente o olhar. É sob essa perspectiva que a segunda edição da NRF Europa, em Paris, ganha interesse para o mercado brasileiro: não apenas pelos conteúdos apresentados nos palcos, mas pela possibilidade de observar o que acontece fora deles — nas ruas, nas lojas, nos novos formatos de negócio e nas escolhas que as marcas estão fazendo diante de um consumidor e de um ambiente regulatório muito particulares. Ao longo dessa cobertura, serão observados alguns desses movimentos: as discussões sobre o futuro do varejo, a experiência concreta das lojas europeias, a presença de marcas brasileiras no mercado internacional e os desafios enfrentados por empresas que atravessam fronteiras em ambas as direções. Mais do que reunir tendências, a proposta é colocar essas referências em perspectiva, porque talvez a pergunta mais interessante não seja o que o varejo europeu tem a ensinar à moda brasileira. Talvez seja o que observar a Europa pode nos fazer enxergar sobre o nosso próprio va

articles.title: Coop estende horário e leva operação 24 horas a 20 supermercados
articles.titleKo: Coop estende horário e leva operação 24 horas a 20 supermercados
articles.originalSummary: A Coop ampliou o atendimento 24 horas para 20 lojas de supermercado, passando a operar ininterruptamente em unidades localizadas no ABC Paulista e nas cidades de Sorocaba, São José dos Campos, Tatuí e Piracicaba. Segundo Celso Furtado, diretor-geral da Coop, as primeiras unidades que passaram a operar no formato 24 horas já apresentam boa aceitação por parte dos cooperados e clientes. De acordo com o executivo, a iniciativa tem permitido observar hábitos de consumo, necessidades específicas dos clientes e oportunidades de aprimoramento da operação. “Ainda estamos em fase de acompanhamento e avaliação dos resultados para entender plenamente o potencial desse modelo”, afirma. A iniciativa busca reforçar a conveniência e acompanha as transformações nos hábitos de consumo e as tendências do varejo. Com horários mais flexíveis, os cooperados e clientes ganham mais opções para realizar suas compras de acordo com a própria rotina, inclusive fora dos períodos convencionais de atendimento. “Os estudos mostram que grande parte desse público é formada por clientes e cooperados já habituados à Coop, que valorizam conveniência e flexibilidade de horário. Também observamos a presença de consumidores que, por rotina de trabalho ou estilo de vida, têm necessidade de realizar compras fora dos horários tradicionais”, afirma Furtado. O executivo afirma que a companhia já observou uma movimentação consistente durante os horários estendidos. “Neste momento, nosso principal objetivo é avaliar o comportamento do consumidor, a aderência ao serviço e a sustentabilidade operacional do modelo”, acrescenta. Expansão do modelo De acordo com Furtado, a expansão do modelo 24 horas da Coop está sendo conduzida de forma gradual e criteriosa, com o monitoramento dos resultados das unidades que já operam nesse formato. “Qualquer decisão de ampliação será baseada em estudos técnicos, nas necessidades dos clientes e na viabilidade operacional de cada região”, explica. Entre os fatores considerados para a implementação do modelo nas unidades da rede estão o perfil da região, o comportamento dos clientes, o fluxo de consumidores, os aspectos operacionais, a segurança e a capacidade de cada unidade de sustentar o modelo de atendimento. A companhia realiza uma análise individual de cada loja com o objetivo de garantir que a decisão esteja alinhada às necessidades dos cooperados e aos objetivos da cooperativa. “Acreditamos que o consumidor busca cada vez mais conveniência e liberdade de escolha. O atendimento 24 horas surge como mais uma alternativa para atender diferentes necessidades e momentos de compra”, diz o diretor-geral da Coop. articles.title: Pizza Prime leva operação aos cinemas e amplia canais para chegar a 600 pontos de venda
articles.titleKo: Pizza Prime leva operação aos cinemas e amplia canais para chegar a 600 pontos de venda
articles.originalSummary: A Pizza Prime ampliou seus canais de venda ao fechar uma parceria com a Cinemark para comercializar pizzas nas bombonieres de 12 complexos da rede, em São Paulo, Belo Horizonte e Uberlândia. A operação leva os produtos da marca para um novo ambiente de venda e integra o plano de expansão da rede, que tem como meta chegar a 600 pontos de venda até 2031. “Essa parceria nos coloca em um novo contexto de consumo, associado ao entretenimento e fora do ambiente tradicional das pizzarias. A iniciativa também amplia a presença da marca e permite que o consumidor tenha contato com a Pizza Prime em diferentes momentos do seu dia, inclusive no cinema”, Gabriel Concon, fundador e CEO da Pizza Prime. Nas unidades participantes, a Cinemark passou a oferecer os sabores Marguerita e Pepperoni. A parceria amplia a presença da Pizza Prime para além das pizzarias e acrescenta o cinema à lista de locais onde os consumidores podem comprar os produtos da marca. “Temos como objetivo atingir 600 pontos de venda até 2031, e ampliar os pontos de contato e as ocasiões de consumo da marca faz parte dessa estratégia de crescimento”, diz. Concon destaca que os resultados superaram a expectativa inicial as vendas nas unidades da Cinemark ficaram 15% acima do projetado no primeiro mês. articles.title: Comissão da ‘MP das blusinhas’ adia novamente votação, agora para a quarta-feira
articles.titleKo: Comissão da ‘MP das blusinhas’ adia novamente votação, agora para a quarta-feira
articles.originalSummary: A comissão mista do Congresso Nacional sobre a “MP das Blusinhas” adiou novamente a votação da proposta. A sessão estava marcada para esta terça-feira, 1º de setembro, e foi remarcada para a quarta-feira, 2, às 10 horas. A Medida Provisória autoriza o Ministério da Fazenda a zerar a “taxa das blusinhas”, imposto sobre compras de até US$ 50 em plataformas estrangeiras. Se não for aprovada até 8 de setembro pela comissão mista e pelos plenários da Câmara dos Deputados e do Senado Federal, a MP perderá a validade. A medida foi assinada pelo presidente da República, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), e o governo teme que o imposto volte a vigorar, em plena campanha eleitoral do petista. À imprensa, a senadora Leila Barros (PDT-DF), relatora da “MP das Blusinhas”, afirmou que vai divulgar o relatório ainda nesta terça, após uma reunião com os presidentes do Congresso Nacional, Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP) e Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), prevista para as 19 horas. Leila disse que a reunião será uma continuidade do encontro que estava marcado para as 14 horas e que não terminou. Além disso, segundo a senadora, há alguns “impasses” sobre o texto. Em relação à discussão sobre garantir exclusividade dos Correios sobre as entregas de produtos isentos de tributação, Leila respondeu: “Não tem consenso, não vou negar”. Setores empresariais também têm pedido compensações por se dizerem prejudicados com uma concorrência injusta diante de plataformas internacionais. Leila afirmou que poderia inserir no texto um mecanismo de reavaliação semestral do fim da “taxa das blusinhas”, a ser realizada pelo Ministério da Fazenda, para verificar a necessidade de apresentar um projeto de mitigação dos impactos econômicos sobre as empresas. Há, no entanto, uma reivindicação do Congresso para que os parlamentares também aprovem a reavaliação periódica. Com informações de Estadão Conteúdo (Victor Ohana). articles.title: Popeyes passa a oferecer Coca-Cola no cardápio de bebidas no Brasil
articles.titleKo: Popeyes passa a oferecer Coca-Cola no cardápio de bebidas no Brasil
articles.originalSummary: O Popeyes passou a oferecer produtos da Coca-Cola em suas unidades no Brasil. A mudança na oferta de bebidas é divulgada pela rede por meio da campanha “Refil Refri agora é Coca-Cola”, estrelada pelo influenciador Pedro Certezas. Produzido pela agência Jota, o filme usa referências ao futebol e apresenta Certezas como um “técnico” que orienta consumidores após os pedidos. Em uma das cenas, ele identifica uma pessoa sem Coca-Cola e faz uma brincadeira sobre a substituição, em alusão a uma partida de futebol. “A chegada da Coca-Cola reflete uma decisão estratégica orientada pela escuta ativa do nosso público. Trata-se de um passo fundamental para fortalecer o posicionamento de Popeyes no mercado”, destaca Lucas Porto, Diretor de Vendas e Marketing de Popeyes. Marca ajuda a impulsionar vendas digitais da Zamp As vendas digitais da Zamp, dona das operações de Burger King, Popeyes, Starbucks e Subway no Brasil, somaram R$ 867 milhões no segundo trimestre de 2026, um crescimento de 26,7% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. O valor, que considera as vendas realizadas por totens de autoatendimento, delivery e aplicativo, representou 65,5% da receita dos restaurantes da companhia. Com crescimento de 23%, os totens de autoatendimento concentraram 56,3% das vendas digitais. As vendas pelo cresceram 39% e atingiram 37% do volume. Já o aplicativo representou 6,7% das vendas digitais. Segundo balanço do segundo trimestre , as vendas digitais alcançaram R$ 867 milhões no período, acima dos R$ 684 milhões registrados no mesmo trimestre de 2025. No período, o Burger King representou 66,1% da venda bruta total do sistema Zamp, que movimentou R$ 2,7 bilhões no trimestre. A marca registrou receita líquida de R$ 1,127 bilhão. articles.title: Gerando Falcões leva bazar itinerante ao metrô com até 80% de desconto
articles.titleKo: Gerando Falcões leva bazar itinerante ao metrô com até 80% de desconto
articles.originalSummary: A Gerando Falcões inaugurou uma unidade de seu bazar itinerante na estação Tatuapé, da Linha 3-Vermelha, em parceria com o Metrô de São Paulo. O espaço, instalado ao lado da bilheteria, oferece roupas, calçados e acessórios com descontos de até 80%. O bazar funciona de segunda a sábado, das 8h às 21h. A renda obtida com as vendas é destinada aos projetos sociais da organização, que atua em mais de 5.500 favelas brasileiras e tem como meta tirar 1 milhão de pessoas da pobreza e levá-las à dignidade. “O bazar aocial é uma maneira de transformar algo que já faz parte da vida das pessoas. Ao mesmo tempo em que incentivamos que roupas e acessórios tenham uma vida mais longa, a renda volta para projetos que trabalham para ampliar oportunidades nas favelas”, afirma Júlia Machado, diretora de Negócios Sociais da Gerando Falcões. A estação Tatuapé foi escolhida pelo alto fluxo de pessoas. O formato itinerante permite que o bazar passe por diferentes locais da cidade e alcance novos públicos. Modelo de franquias A Gerando Falcões expandiu sua presença no Brasil para mais de 6 mil comunidades por meio do modelo de franquia social. A implementação desse formato é uma parceria com a Cherto Consultoria, tradicionalmente associado ao setor empresarial, mas agora utilizado por ONGs para ampliar o impacto de suas ações. Conhecido como “franquia social” ou “ONG acelerada”, o modelo oferece uma estrutura padronizada que permite a replicação de práticas bem-sucedidas em diferentes localidades, contribuindo para a multiplicação de resultados e o fortalecimento da credibilidade junto a doadores e parceiros. “A franquia social é uma forma de gerenciar o ecossistema de ONGs de maneira padronizada e eficiente”, afirma Marcelo Cherto, da Cherto Consultoria e um dos fundadores da Associação Brasileira de Franquias ( ABF ). articles.title: Com assistente Sofia, Decolar faz primeira venda 100% por IA com pagamento via Pix
articles.titleKo: Com assistente Sofia, Decolar faz primeira venda 100% por IA com pagamento via Pix
articles.originalSummary: A Decolar realizou no Brasil sua primeira venda 100% agêntica, em formato de conversa e com apoio da Sofia, assistente virtual de viagens da empresa desenvolvida com Inteligência Artificial generativa. A venda ocorreu menos de 12 horas após a ativação do recurso. Nesse modelo, o cliente faz a compra em uma única conversa, com a transação conduzida pela IA e a confirmação do pagamento via Pix feita pelo próprio usuário. “Já enxergávamos que o próximo passo seria ter agentes capazes de executar uma venda do início ao fim, trazendo mais segurança para a decisão, reduzindo fricção na jornada e salvando tempo do consumidor. A IA não pode ser tecnologia pela tecnologia. Ela precisa gerar valor de fato e consequentemente, resultado para o negócio. Se não, é só hyppe”, diz Rafaela Rezende, CEO da Decolar. Nessa primeira transação, o cliente buscou uma hospedagem e a Sofia apresentou opções de acordo com suas preferências. Após a escolha, a assistente conduziu o viajante pelas etapas para concluir a reserva, exibiu os dados da transação e disponibilizou o QR Code para pagamento. Sem sair da conversa, o usuário realizou o Pix e, após a confirmação, a reserva foi efetivada. Com o novo recurso, o pagamento é realizado dentro da própria conversa, sem a necessidade de acessar outro ambiente. A solução está em fase de testes, e essa primeira experiência permite avaliar seu funcionamento em uma situação real antes da ampliação da aplicação. Os próximos passos incluem outros produtos de viagem, além da hospedagem, e novos meios de pagamento , além do Pix. Sofia expande presença Lançada em março de 2024, a Sofia já interage com 45% dos viajantes em algum momento da jornada, seja na inspiração e no planejamento, durante a viagem ou após seu término. A assistente registra cerca de 2 milhões de conversas por mês, e 6,7% do faturamento total da Decolar já está associado a interações com a ferramenta. Em dois anos, a Sofia passou a atuar em diferentes etapas da jornada do viajante, da inspiração e do planejamento ao pós-venda e, agora, à execução da compra. articles.title: Nova regra do Pix amplia prazo para contestar golpe
articles.titleKo: Nova regra do Pix amplia prazo para contestar golpe
articles.originalSummary: Uma nova regra do Pix amplia, a partir desta terça-feira, 1, de 30 para 80 dias o prazo para contestar uma devolução realizada pelo Mecanismo Especial de Devolução (MED) quando houver suspeita de fraude. A mudança foi estabelecida pelo Banco Central e busca proteger principalmente comerciantes, prestadores de serviço e pequenos negócios vítimas de golpes que usam o próprio sistema de segurança do Pix. O novo prazo vale para quem recebeu um Pix de forma legítima, mas teve o dinheiro devolvido posteriormente por causa de uma contestação considerada fraudulenta. A contagem começa na data da devolução feita pelo MED. O prazo para quem enviou um Pix e foi vítima de fraude continua sendo de 80 dias, contados a partir da transação original. Dois prazos Com a mudança, há duas situações distintas em que o prazo é de 80 dias: Vítima que enviou o Pix: tem até 80 dias a partir da transferência para pedir o MED; Recebedor que sofreu devolução indevida: tem até 80 dias a partir da devolução para contestá-la. A alteração está prevista na Instrução Normativa BCB 766 , que atualizou o Manual Operacional do Diretório de Identificadores de Contas Transacionais (DICT), integrante das regras do Pix. Golpe contra lojistas A mudança mira uma fraude que explora o mecanismo de proteção do Pix. O golpista pode fazer um pagamento para uma loja ou prestador de serviço e, depois, alegar que transferiu o dinheiro por engano. Ele pede que o comerciante devolva o valor por uma nova transferência, muitas vezes para uma chave diferente. Depois, o criminoso aciona o MED no próprio banco e afirma que o pagamento original foi resultado de fraude. Se a contestação for aceita e houver saldo disponível, o valor pode ser devolvido pelo banco. Nesse cenário, o comerciante pode acabar perdendo dinheiro duas vezes: primeiro ao fazer uma nova transferência e depois com a devolução do Pix original. Por isso, a recomendação é utilizar a função de devolução vinculada à própria transação no aplicativo do banco, em vez de fazer um novo Pix para uma chave informada pela outra pessoa. Como funciona O MED foi criado para facilitar a recuperação de valores em casos de fraude, golpe, crime ou falha operacional. O mecanismo, porém, não serve para cancelar qualquer Pix. Não estão incluídos casos como: Arrependimento de uma compra; Erro de valor cometido pelo próprio usuário; Erro na escolha da chave Pix; Simples desacordo comercial sem indício de fraude. Ao identificar uma fraude, o usuário deve procurar o banco e solicitar a abertura do MED. As instituições analisam o caso e, no fluxo de fraude, têm até sete dias para verificar se há indícios de irregularidade. Se a fraude for confirmada, a devolução depende da existência de recursos disponíveis nas contas envolvidas e pode ser total ou parcial. MED 2.0 A ampliação do prazo ocorre em meio à implantação do chamado MED 2.0, versão mais robusta do mecanismo de devolução. Desde fevereiro de 2026, o sistema permite rastrear o caminho percorrido pelo dinheiro depois que ele é transferido para outras contas. Antes, a recuperação ficava mais concentrada na conta que havia recebido originalmente os recursos. O novo modelo pode aumentar as chances de bloqueio e recuperação mesmo quando o dinheiro é movimentado entre diferentes contas. A devolução, entretanto, não é garantida: se os recursos já tiverem sido sacados, transferidos novamente ou não houver saldo disponível, a recuperação pode ser prejudicada. Uma etapa adicional de comunicação entre as instituições, inicialmente prevista para agosto, foi adiada para 26 de outubro. Segundo o Banco Central, a alteração não muda o funcionamento do rastreamento já disponível. Se cair no golpe Quem perceber que foi vítima de fraude deve procurar o banco o mais rápido possível, mesmo que ainda esteja dentro do prazo de 80 dias. A rapidez aumenta a possibilidade de encontrar recursos disponíveis para bloqueio. Também é importante guardar: Comprovante da transferência; Conversas e mensagens; Anúncios ou

articles.title: Apps avançam no transporte corporativo e já chegam a 50% das empresas
articles.titleKo: Apps avançam no transporte corporativo e já chegam a 50% das empresas
articles.originalSummary: A utilização de aplicativos de mobilidade já faz parte da rotina de 50% das empresas nos deslocamentos corporativos. O percentual supera o registrado entre veículos locados, utilizados por 48% das companhias, fretados, por 47%, e frota própria, por 40%, segudo dados de uma pesquisa da 99 para Empresas em parceria com o Datafolha. As empresas também combinam diferentes modalidades de transporte para as atividades profissionais. Segundo o levantamento, são utilizadas, em média, três opções de deslocamento por companhia. Para os próximos 12 meses, os aplicativos de mobilidade aparecem como a modalidade mais citada pelas empresas que pretendem ampliar o uso, com 34% das respostas. O percentual é mais que o dobro do registrado pelos veículos fretados, com 16%. Na sequência estão os veículos locados, com 14%, e a frota própria, com 12%. Quando consideradas as modalidades que já fazem parte da rotina das empresas, os aplicativos são mencionados por 22% das companhias. Os veículos fretados e a frota própria aparecem com 18% cada. A pesquisa também aponta que 58% das empresas pretendem aumentar o uso de soluções de mobilidade corporativa nos próximos 12 meses. Outros 40% afirmam que devem manter o nível atual, enquanto 3% indicam uma redução. Entre as empresas que gastam mais de R$ 25 mil por mês com mobilidade corporativa, a intenção de ampliar o uso chega a 64%. Solução digital e gastos As soluções digitais ganham espaço na gestão dos deslocamentos. Entre as 113 empresas pesquisadas que utilizam aplicativos de mobilidade e/ou serviços de táxi, 62% usam aplicativos vinculados à conta corporativa, à frente do reembolso de despesas (51%), cartão corporativo (46%) e solicitações feitas por uma área responsável (46%). Entre as empresas com mais de 100 deslocamentos corporativos por mês, o uso de aplicativos vinculados à conta corporativa chega a 71%, ante 52% entre aquelas com até 100 deslocamentos mensais. Considerando o total da amostra, 57% utilizam centros de custo para controlar as despesas com mobilidade, 44% adotam prestação de contas ou justificativas dos deslocamentos e 43% utilizam relatórios periódicos de utilização e gastos. Aprovação prévia e regras de utilização por horário, localidade ou finalidade são adotadas por 41% das empresas, cada uma. Na escolha dos fornecedores, segurança dos colaboradores (41%) e preço ou custo (40%) são os principais aspectos considerados pelas empresas. Na sequência, aparecem agilidade no atendimento e tempo de espera (27%), qualidade do atendimento e suporte (23%), facilidade de uso para os colaboradores (23%), credibilidade e reputação da empresa (23%) e cobertura geográfica e disponibilidade de veículos (21%). A mobilidade corporativa é considerada essencial em algum nível por 93% das empresas pesquisadas. Para 51%, ela é parte essencial da atividade principal da companhia, enquanto 42% afirmam que é essencial para algumas áreas. articles.title: How an Industry Outsider Rewired an Iconic Restaurant Empire
articles.titleKo: How an Industry Outsider Rewired an Iconic Restaurant Empire
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Nearly 30 years ago, Blackbird helped kick off a shift in Midwestern dining. The restaurant was set in Chicago’s then-gritty West Loop and looked nothing like the white-tablecloth rooms the city was used to. But by pairing high-caliber technique with an approachable and vibrant minimalist setting, it helped pull fine dining out of its formal past while offering a new, modern blueprint for farm-to-table cuisine. Blackbird’s runaway success helped lay the foundation for what would become One Off Hospitality, a trailblazing collection of restaurants and defining force in Chicago’s food scene. From the rustic, communal warmth of avec and the beer-and-pork-laden halls of The Publican to the honky-tonk energy of Big Star and the craft cocktail precision of The Violet Hour, the group has helped reshape the independent dining landscape with its array of concepts over the years. Along the way it has earned nine James Beard Awards, Michelin recognition, and widespread acclaim. And its kitchens have produced a generation of chefs who have gone on to make their own marks on the industry, cementing One Off’s status as an institution in American dining. Which is why, at first glance, the appointment of Karen Browne as the company’s first-ever CEO in 2019 seemed like an unexpected choice. Here you had an influential restaurant group, known for operating hugely successful spots in one of the world’s most celebrated food cities. And the woman stepping in to steer the ship was a total newcomer to hospitality. But nearly eight years after hiring an outsider to lead an insider institution, One Off is thinking bigger than it ever has before. It has started to look less like a collection of concepts and more like a hospitality ecosystem—restaurants, yes, but also catering and events, partnerships, and other touchpoints that extend its culinary prowess beyond the dining room. Behind the scenes, it’s a more disciplined company than it used to be. There’s tighter reporting, clearer systems, and a framework designed to protect what made these places successful while making room to grow across The Windy City, the suburbs, and eventually beyond. Courtesy of K Rosales Photography The Fixer Steps Inside To understand how Browne set out to professionalize a chef-driven empire, it helps to start with where she came from. She arrived at One Off with deep executive experience leading some of the country’s largest human capital organizations, including a decade-long run as president of PeopleScout. There, she helped turn the Chicago-based firm into a global hiring force by “building a system that leveraged scalability and centralization” to make recruiting more efficient without stripping out the human element. Later, she was tapped to lead Advantage xPO, where she consolidated dozens of struggling staffing firms into a handful of brands and steered the company through its sale to Recruit, the HR giant behind platforms like Indeed and Glassdoor. From there she served as president and COO of EG Workforce Solutions before launching her own consulting and creative firm. Mo’ Bettahs announced the promotion of Kylee Arreaga to Vice President of Marketing, recognizing two years of leadership that have strengthened the Hawaiian-style fast-casual brand’s marketing organization as it accelerates its national growth. Arreaga joined Mo’ Bettahs in September 2024 as Senior Director of Marketing, stepping into a marketing team that was already doing strong work for the brand. In the two years since, she has built it into a full-service department, adding talented people across paid media, owned media, social media, customer service and Makana Rewards, the loyalty program that now counts nearly 750,000 members and keeps Mo’ Bettahs connected to its most loyal guests. Growing our own leaders matters to us just as much as growing our footprint, and Kylee is exactly the kind of leader we want driving this brand forward.” “Getting to help build something this special has been the honor of my career,” said Arreaga. “Mo’ Bettahs is a category-defining brand, and I’ve watched it grow from a local favorite into a name people drive across town for, without ever losing the Aloha that makes it what it is. articles.title: 7 Brew Wins Auction for 73 Salad and Go Sites in $143 Million Deal
articles.titleKo: 7 Brew Wins Auction for 73 Salad and Go Sites in $143 Million Deal
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . 7 Brew has over 800 locations in the U.S. 7 Brew has won the competition for a large portfolio of Salad and Go real estate, agreeing to pay roughly $143.2 million for 73 sites as the drive-thru salad chain moves through bankruptcy . Salad and Go conducted an auction Monday between 7 Brew and Dutch Bros. The company entered the proceedings with 7 Brew as the lead bidder, and Dutch Bros ultimately elected not to submit a topping bid, according to bankruptcy court documents. Salad and Go subsequently named 7 Brew the successful bidder and Dutch Bros the backup bidder. The 73-site portfolio includes 41 locations in Arizona, 20 in Texas, and six each in Nevada and Oklahoma, according to court documents. 7 Brew is one of the fastest-growing concepts in America. It now has over 800 locations in 38 states. The company opened a net of 562 shops across 2023, 2024, and 2025. It earned $1.2 billion in sales last year and posted a $2.6 million AUV. READ MORE : Dutch Bros and 7 Brew to Battle for Salad and Go Locations Dutch Bros Strikes $105 Million Deal for Salad and Go Locations The outcome marks a significant turn from the transaction Salad and Go proposed when it filed for bankruptcy on August 4. Dutch Bros initially agreed to pay $105 million for 51 drive-thru restaurants in Arizona and Nevada, along with 14 leases in Texas and Oklahoma. But Salad and Go’s bankruptcy process left the door open for a higher offer. 7 Brew subsequently emerged as a competing bidder, setting up a head-to-head auction between two of the fastest-growing drive-thru beverage concepts in the country. Dutch Bros is entitled to a $3.8 million termination fee, plus reasonable and documented expenses, if the 7 Brew transaction closes. The final portfolio could still change before closing. 7 Brew can drop certain leases if it can’t operate its business at those locations. The sale comes after a dramatic retrenchment for Salad and Go. The brand, founded in Gilbert, Arizona, in 2013, had expanded to 146 restaurants at its peak before beginning a widespread closure program. Roughly 70 restaurants were slated for closure as the company pulled out of Texas and Oklahoma and concentrated its remaining operations in Arizona and Nevada. The restructuring also included the closure of its Garland, Texas, commissary. The contraction followed an aggressive period of development that left Salad and Go facing financial pressure. The company raised approximately $27 million in additional capital between December 2025 and January 2026 before ultimately filing for bankruptcy. 7 Brew’s winning bid gives the beverage chain access to dozens of existing drive-thru sites at a time when competition for suitable real estate has intensified across the industry. The transaction isn’t final. A court hearing is scheduled for September 21 to consider the transfer of the leases and contracts to 7 Brew. articles.title: Panera Unveils Fall Menu with New Soups, Sweets, and Returning Favorites
articles.titleKo: Panera Unveils Fall Menu with New Soups, Sweets, and Returning Favorites
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Panera's latest menu innovations are available for dine-in, delivery, Rapid Pick-Up, or drive-thru at Panera Bread bakery-cafes nationwide beginning September 2. The days are getting cooler, the cravings are getting cozier, and that can only mean one thing: Panera Season is here. Today, Panera Bread is officially welcoming fall with a flavor-packed menu designed to deliver guests the ultimate cozy comfort. Just in time for back-to-school routines and crisp autumn days, Panera’s fall lineup features the flavors guests crave most, including warm sandwiches, hearty new soups, the seasonal Harvest Medley Salad, and the return of guest favorites like the Chocolate Chip Bagel and Ciabatta Dippers. When the weather cools down, there’s only one place to go: Panera. Panera’s signature fall soups are back, led by the new Three-Cheese Lasagna Soup, featuring a rich ricotta-tomato broth. Guests can also enjoy the return of Panera’s comforting seasonal soup lineup, including: NEW Three-Cheese Lasagna Soup : Italian-style sausage, lasagna ribbon pasta, and parmesan cheese, in a ricotta tomato broth topped with asiago cheese. Rustic Baked Potato Soup : Homestyle-cut potatoes, bacon and chives in a seasoned creamy broth topped with even more bacon. Autumn Squash Soup : A seasonal fan favorite, featuring a rich blend of butternut squash and pumpkin simmered in vegetable broth with select ingredients, with honey, cinnamon and a hint of curry, finished with sweet cream and topped with roasted pumpkin seeds. Nothing pairs better with Panera’s fall soups than warm, hearty sandwiches, and returning for the season is the ultimate companion for dipping: Ciabatta Dippers. Inspired by guests who love to dip their sandwiches into every last spoonful of soup, Ciabatta Dippers bring the best of both together in one craveable offering. Embrace the dip in two distinct varieties with the French Ciabatta Dipper and Chicken Pesto Ciabatta Dipper. The seasonal Ciabatta Dippers are a delicious addition to Panera’s warm sandwich lineup, featuring guest favorites including the Chipotle Chicken Avocado Melt, the Toasted Italiano and the Chicken Bacon Rancher. To satisfy every sweet tooth, Panera is delivering beloved flavor combinations in unexpected ways, including a new, seasonal PB&J Cookie – a fresh take on a childhood favorite, featuring a soft peanut butter cookie with a gooey grape jelly filling. Panera’s fall bakery lineup includes: NEW PB&J Cookie – Peanut butter cookie filled with grape jelly and dusted with powdered sugar NEW Cinnamon Croissant Bites – Mini croissants baked with our sweet cinnamon crunch topping and served with a side of icing. IT’S BACK! Chocolate Chip Bagel – More bagels, more fun. Reintroducing the Chocolate Chip Bagel back on Panera’s menu. “When the temperature drops, Panera is the place to go – we’ve crafted a seasonal fall menu that brings warm comfort, nostalgia and exciting new flavors to every occasion,” said Scott Uehlein, Vice President of Culinary, Panera Bread. “From the hearty warmth of our new Three-Cheese Lasagna Soup to the playful joy of our PB&J Cookie, we’re bringing everything our guests love about the season to the menu. We’re also excited to bring back our beloved Chocolate Chip Bagel, delivering the familiar flavors and traditions our guests look forward to each fall.” Rounding out the seasonal menu is the return of the crisp and colorful Harvest Medley Salad, featuring an abundance of delicious toppings that truly capture the taste of the season, including a bed of mixed greens and fresh arugula, pumpkin seeds, mandarin oranges and crunchy beet strips. From crisp mornings and sweater weather to warm lunches and comforting dinners, the best fall moments are made even better at Panera. articles.title: Wetzel’s Pretzels and sweetFrog to Open New Co-Branded Store in Flower Mound, Texas
articles.titleKo: Wetzel’s Pretzels and sweetFrog to Open New Co-Branded Store in Flower Mound, Texas
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Wetzel’s Pretzels (Wetzel’s), the iconic brand known for fresh, hand-rolled pretzels, is teaming up with sweetFrog to bring a new co-branded destination to Flower Mound. Located at 2500 Cross Timbers Rd, Suite 110, the new store will give families and guests throughout North Texas a convenient place to enjoy warm, freshly baked pretzels and premium frozen treats all under one roof. Local entrepreneurs and husband-and-wife duo Dave and Diana Stone will lead operations at the co-branded Flower Mound location. Dave has more than two decades of experience in logistics, transportation, and freight brokerage. Diana brings a diverse professional background that includes experience as a registered nurse in intensive care and work at a nationwide law firm. The Stones will serve the Flower Mound community, create a welcoming destination for local families, and continue growing their business portfolio. “We were drawn to the co-brand concept because it brings two great brands together and gives guests the best of both worlds in one convenient location,” said Dave. “We’re incredibly proud to become part of the Flower Mound community and create a fun, welcoming place where families and friends can come together to enjoy fresh pretzels, frozen treats, and memorable moments.” The co-brand model provides flexibility for Wetzel’s Pretzels and sweetFrog franchisees, featuring an adaptable buildout design that integrates seamlessly into a variety of footprints. As Wetzel’s continues to expand in non-traditional spaces, its store-within-a-store format pairs naturally with sweetFrog to maximize efficiency and enhance the guest experience. The combination also strengthens daypart performance, appealing to both snack-driven and dessert-focused occasions. Together, the brands offer franchisees a proven system and an opportunity to diversify while scaling for long-term growth. “We’re looking forward to bringing together Wetzel’s Pretzels and sweetFrog to create a one-of-a-kind destination for guests,” said Eric Weigel, Brand Leader of Wetzel’s Pretzels. “The continued expansion of our co-brand model demonstrates the versatility of the concept, allowing both brands to reach even more communities across the country. We’re confident Dave and Diana’s entrepreneurial spirit, diverse professional backgrounds, and commitment to their community will make this location a favorite for local families.” Wetzel’s has been sharing its signature handheld happiness since its founding in Pasadena, California, in 1994. The brand continues to attract a devoted following in communities across North America through its cool SoCal feel and crave-worthy snacks that create special moments of pure pretzel bliss among friends, family, and colleagues. For additional information about Wetzel’s franchise opportunities, visit wetzelsfranchising.com. articles.title: Perkins Announces Franchise Incentives for Myrtle Beach Market
articles.titleKo: Perkins Announces Franchise Incentives for Myrtle Beach Market
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Perkins Restaurant and Bakery, a leading family-dining restaurant brand known for its homestyle meals, all day value, and iconic bakery, is teaming up with the City of Myrtle Beach to attract new business in the bustling resort city. To sweeten the deal, Perkins is extending an exclusive incentive package featuring reduced royalty fees for a limited time to new franchisee signings, and the city of Myrtle Beach is offering a Facade Improvement Grant which provides a dollar-for-dollar matching grant of up to $10,000 per project. “Myrtle Beach provides incredible growth potential for franchisees,” said Peter Ortiz, Chief Development Officer for Ascent Hospitality Management, the parent company of Perkins Restaurant & Bakery. “Our incentive package, along with the business-friendly local government, makes it even more appealing for prospective partners to open a restaurant in this expanding community.” The Perks of Opening in Myrtle Beach The popular South Carolina seaside city offers a number of attractive reasons for opening a Perkins restaurant. Top of the list is its strong year-round tourism traffic. The city brings in more than 18 million visitors a year. A large share of the Myrtle Beach visitors are families, an audience that aligns with the brand’s longstanding heritage of breakfast and bakery offerings. Myrtle Beach is considered a vibrant hub of the Grand Strand, a continuous 60-mile stretch of beaches in the northeastern part of South Carolina that is one of the country’s fastest growing populations. Known for its beach activities, the city also offers a variety of entertainment and attractions that extend beyond the shores for residents and vacationers alike. “Myrtle Beach is excited to welcome Perkins to our outstanding selection of restaurants here along The Grand Strand,” said Mayor Mark Kruea, City of Myrtle Beach. “Our residents and millions of visitors always enjoy great food in a great atmosphere. The Myrtle Beach area is ready when you are.” Plating Up For Success Perkins brings a strong legacy spanning more than 65 years. As a beloved family dining destination known for serving classic American meals, the brand has a presence in the U.S. and Canada with more than 250 locations and growing. The company continues to attract new franchisees through its flexible build options that meet partners at their business goals. Partners also receive comprehensive support throughout their Perkins journey from the early phases with real estate selection and planning to marketing, operations, and training that help ensure a successful opening and beyond. “As we expand our presence across the country, we continue to strengthen our franchise program that is spotlighted with a proven business model and a system of franchisees who share our passion for quality food and exceptional hospitality,” said Ortiz. The reduced royalty fees for new signings is available to qualifying franchisees. The incentive is valid through December 2026. The City of North Myrtle Beach Façade Grant Program provides matching funds to support exterior improvements to existing commercial buildings. To learn more about eligibility, visit https://www.nmb.us/829/Facade-Grant-Program. To learn more about Perkins Restaurant & Bakery, including franchising opportunities, visit https://perkinsfranchising.com. articles.title: Michelin-Trained Chefs Alex Catotti and Erin Kobler Plan Durham, North Carolina, Restaurants
articles.titleKo: Michelin-Trained Chefs Alex Catotti and Erin Kobler Plan Durham, North Carolina, Restaurants
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chef Alex Catotti is coming home. After building a career in some of the country’s most celebrated kitchens, the Durham native will return to his hometown with his wife and business partner Pastry Chef Erin Kobler to open Restaurant Cornelia, the fine dining destination he has dreamed of for years. The pair will also open a sister concept, The Vintner and The Baker, to serve as the backbone of the chefs’ sustainable mission. Together, Restaurant Cornelia and The Vintner and The Baker will place Durham at the forefront of the culinary scene in the American South. The restaurants will share the same downtown Durham address at 949 Washington Street and are slated to open in Spring 2027. Visit corneliadurham.com and follow @restaurantcornelia, @vintnerbaker and the chefs at @alex_catotti and @erincobbler. Catotti most recently served as Sous Chef at the three-Michelin-star Smyth in Chicago — ranked the No. 1 restaurant in North America by The World’s 50 Best. His path there began in Durham, training under Chef Scott Howell at Nana’s, and continued in California at Restaurant Trokay before he immersed himself in Chicago’s celebrated fine dining scene. Over nearly a decade, he also honed his craft at the one-Michelin-starred Next, and at Bellemore, part of acclaimed chef-driven Boka Restaurant Group. Now, he returns to the community that shaped him, bringing with him the elevated craft and hospitality that define Chicago’s fine dining scene. Kobler brings her own distinguished pedigree to the project, most recently serving as Executive Pastry Chef at Sepia and Proxi in Chicago, where she directed the pastry program for the Michelin-starred tasting menu restaurant and its globally inspired Bib Gourmand sister property — work that earned her a 2024 Jean Banchet Award nomination for Best Pastry Chef in Chicago and recognition as a 2024 StarChefs Rising Star. She built her foundation on the opening team at Boka Restaurant Group’s Bellemore, named one of Robb Report’s “10 Best New Restaurants in America,” and is a Chef Ambassador for Nielsen-Massey Vanillas. Together, Catotti and Kobler have worked alongside some of Chicago’s most acclaimed chefs and restaurateurs, including John and Karen Shields of Smyth and The Loyalist, Grant Achatz of Alinea and Next, Andrew Zimmerman of Sepia and Proxi, and Jimmy Papadopolous and Leigh Omilinsky, formerly of the Boka Restaurant Group. Restaurant Cornelia takes its name from the Chicago street where Alex and Erin shared their first home together — a quiet nod to the formative years that shaped them, and that they now carry home with them to Durham. Here, they’ll introduce a seasonal, rotating tasting menu built around the fermentation and preservation of local ingredients, drawing on partnerships with farmers, fishers and ranchers across North Carolina and the American South. The Vintner and The Baker, its approachable sister concept within the same space, will transition from a coffee shop and bakery by day, with a menu that reflects Kobler’s award-winning pastry background and their shared love of coffee, and transition into a full-service wine bar by night, offering creative small plates designed to be enjoyed alongside an extensive, natural and low-intervention wine list. “Durham has always had a storied restaurant history and a community of genuinely passionate growers and eaters. I’ve wanted to be part of that story for a long time, and I knew that when I was ready, I wanted to bring back everything I’ve learned working alongside some of the world’s best chefs. With the bounty of what’s around us, we believe we have everything we need for a world-class table,” explained Alex Catotti. “Erin and I can’t wait to share this next chapter with the community that started it all for me as a chef.” Mattie Beason of Elm Partners co-brokered the lease, bringing Restaurant Cornelia and

This fall, Patina Restaurant Group’s Orlando restaurants at Disney Springs are proud to partner with Cookies for Kids’ Cancer for a two-month-campaign dedicated to raising awareness and support for pediatric cancer. From September 1 through October 31, Maria & Enzo’s, Enzo’s Hideaway and The Edison at Disney Springs will offer specialty desserts featuring a house-made ginger snap cookie. A portion of proceeds from each featured dessert sold will benefit the national nonprofit dedicated to funding research for new, improved and less toxic treatments for childhood cancer. Patina’s participating restaurants will offer the following specialty desserts: Maria & Enzo’s: Coppa di Maria and Gelato, featuring vanilla, chocolate and pistachio gelato, sweet Amarena cherries and a house-made ginger snap cookie Enzo’s Hideaway: Coppa di Maria and Gelato, featuring vanilla, chocolate and pistachio gelato, sweet Amarena cherries and a house-made ginger snap cookie The Edison: Dulce de leche cheesecake and house-made gelato topped with a ginger snap cookie “We are incredibly proud to partner with an organization that supports so many children battling pediatric cancer,” said Michael Gabriel, Executive Pastry Chef at Patina Restaurant Group. “Across our three restaurant concepts, our house-made ginger snap cookie will allow our guests a delicious way to help make a meaningful impact.” With pediatric cancer remaining one of the leading causes of disease-related death in children, this campaign serves as a powerful call to action – bringing together teams, guests, and communities in a shared mission to fund research, support families, and spread hope. September is shaping up to be another big reason to grab a cup at PJ’s Coffee. The New Orleans-born brand is inviting guests to celebrate their love of coffee while getting a taste of the city where it began through a lineup of coffee offers, app-exclusive deals and an opportunity to go on an unforgettable adventure for two in honor of National Coffee Day, Sept. 29. Beginning Sept. 1, guests can enter Sip Your Way to a New Orleans Experience for the chance to win a getaway for two during Jazz Fest (April 22-25, 2027) and the Zurich Classic (April 19-25, 2027). One lucky pair will be able to immerse themselves in the heart and soul of New Orleans through its sights, sounds, flavors and culture — the same place PJ’s Coffee has proudly called home for more than 45 years. The prize includes round-trip airfare and hotel accommodations, dining credit, a private tour of PJ’s roasting facility and tickets to both Jazz Fest and the Zurich Classic. Guests can enter through Sept. 30 at pjscoffee.com/neworleansexperience . “Coffee and New Orleans have always been deeply connected, and that spirit is at the heart of everything we do at PJ’s Coffee,” said Felton Jones, Chief Roastmaster for PJ’s Coffee. “National Coffee Day is a great opportunity to celebrate that connection with our guests, whether they’re enjoying their favorite PJ’s beverage in one of our cafés or brewing our coffee at home.” The celebration continues at PJ’s Coffee locations, starting with a free 12-ounce drip coffee with the purchase of any bag of whole bean coffee, available in-store all month long — a nod to PJ’s deep coffee roots and its commitment to sharing its signature roasts with guests. From there, each week highlights a different expression of PJ’s coffee craft through offers for guests to explore the brand’s specialty beverages: Sept. 8 — Hand-Crafted Coffee (app exclusive): Save $1 on any handcrafted espresso beverage, hot or iced, all day. Sept. 15 — Taste of New Orleans (app exclusive): Enjoy any 24-ounce Iced New Orleans Favorite for just $5.04 all day. Sept. 22 — Frozen Happy Hour (app exclusive): Save $2 on any 24-ounce Velvet Ice or Granita from 1-5 p.m., while supplies last. Sept. 29 — National Coffee Day (in-store only): Enjoy a free 12-ounce hot drip coffee or 16-ounce cold brew with any food purchase. articles.title: Lou Malnati’s Announces Third Annual Dessert to Donate Campaign
articles.titleKo: Lou Malnati’s Announces Third Annual Dessert to Donate Campaign
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Lou Malnati’s Pizzeria is inviting guests to satisfy their sweet tooth while supporting a meaningful cause through its third annual Dessert to Donate campaign. Throughout September, Lou Malnati’s will donate $1 from every dessert purchased to the Lou Malnati’s Cancer Research Foundation, helping fund cancer research, patient care and family support services. The campaign is part of Lou Malnati’s annual September fundraising efforts, which also include in-store giving opportunities and the 54th annual Lou Malnati’s Cancer Research Benefit. “For more than five decades, our guests, team members and the community have come together to support a cause that means so much to our family,” said Marc Malnati, owner of Lou Malnati’s. “Every dessert purchased, donation made and ticket sold helps advance cancer research and provide support for patients and families navigating cancer. We’re incredibly grateful to everyone who continues to make an impact through these efforts.” Guests can support the campaign by purchasing any dessert throughout September. Featured offerings include Lou’s handmade Tiramisu, made with espresso-soaked ladyfinger cookies, mascarpone cheese and cocoa powder, and Chocolate Obsession, layered with brownie, mascarpone chocolate mousse and chocolate ganache. In addition to Dessert to Donate, guests can support the Lou Malnati’s Cancer Research Foundation throughout September by purchasing donation circles at any Lou Malnati’s location or rounding up their bill at checkout. Supporters can also attend the 54th Annual Lou Malnati’s Cancer Research Benefit on Sept. 26 at The Aura Club in Naperville. The event will feature dinner, entertainment, auctions and raffle prizes including a chance to win a 1996 Corvette. Event tickets, raffle tickets, and donations are available through LMCB.org . One of Chicago’s longest-running charitable fundraising events, Lou Malnati’s Cancer Research Benefit began in 1971 when Lou Malnati launched the fundraiser in honor of his friend, Chicago Bears player Brian Piccolo. Following Lou’s death from cancer in 1978, the Lou Malnati’s Cancer Research Foundation was established to continue his legacy and today supports the Lou and Jean Malnati Brain Tumor Institute at Northwestern Memorial Hospital, Gilda’s Club Chicago and Pickles Group. Since its founding, the Lou Malnati’s Cancer Research Foundation has helped fund cancer research, treatment and support services for patients and families facing cancer. Available for a limited time beginning September 1, guests can enjoy the Biscoff Flavor Collection in-shop or order ahead through the BR App. Baskin-Robbins is bringing a taste of travel to fall with the launch of the new limited-time Biscoff Flavor Collection, available nationwide beginning September 1, while supplies last. Long associated as the iconic cookie often enjoyed on flights, Biscoff now takes center stage in a lineup of indulgent desserts designed to turn everyday occasions into something worth savoring. Headlined by the brand-new flavor, Biscoff Crème Brûlée Ice Cream, the collection transforms the beloved taste of Biscoff cookies into a lineup of elevated desserts to take autumn vibes up a notch all season long. For many, Biscoff is the iconic cookie that sparks memories of takeoff, window seats, and anticipation for the journey ahead. Now, Baskin-Robbins is capturing the same sense of indulgent escape with a collection that tastes like arriving at a cozy European café, one spoonful at a time. Inspired by the rich flavors of crème brûlée and the unmistakable taste of Biscoff cookies, the collection offers a delicious escape that feels both comforting and elevated. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . WOWorks, the parent company of better-for-you restaurant brands Saladworks, Frutta Bowls , Garbanzo Mediterranean Fresh, The Simple Greek, Barberitos and Zoup! Eatery, today announced it has opened 23 new restaurants so far this year, with 15 additional locations currently in development. This brings WOWorks’ total footprint to nearly 240 restaurants nationwide and puts the company on pace for nearly 40 new stores by year’s end, fueled largely by surging consumer demand for fresh, customizable, better-for-you dining. Nationwide Franchise Expansion New restaurants have launched across the Midwest, Mid-Atlantic and Southeast – including Ohio, Missouri, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Florida, Alabama, Virginia, Georgia and Texas – as well as WOWorks’ first expansion into Canada, with a new Frutta Bowls location in Cambridge, Ontario. Growth spans traditional retail footprints as well as high-traffic non-traditional venues, including university campuses at the University of Georgia’s Tate Student Center and the University of Notre Dame, as well as a healthcare facility debut at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center. “Consumers today want food that fits their life: fresh, customizable and genuinely good for them,” said Kelly Roddy, CEO of WOWorks. “That’s exactly what WOWorks was built for, and it’s why our brands are resonating with guests from coast to coast as we open new doors nearly every week in a multitude of venues.” Co-Branding Fuels Efficient, High-Impact Growth Co-branded restaurants account for nearly half of the openings year-to-date. Pairings such as Saladworks and Frutta Bowls and Barberitos and Garbanzo Mediterranean Fresh, allow WOWorks and its franchisees to serve more craveable, complementary menus under one roof, maximizing real estate efficiency and giving guests more reasons to visit. Several existing single-brand restaurants have also added Frutta Bowls as a second brand this year, a conversion strategy designed to drive incremental revenue from proven locations. “We’re excited to see so many of our franchisees continue to expand within the WOWorks platform,” added Roddy. “They are doubling down on brands they already know deliver results and picking up new brands that fit within spaces they already are operating.” Riding the Wave of Healthy, Customizable Dining WOWorks’ expansion arrives as consumer demand for healthy, customizable dining reaches an all-time high. Guests increasingly want food that fits their lifestyle and dietary restrictions, such as build-your-own bowls, fresh produce and healthy options without sacrificing convenience. WOWorks’ portfolio is built for this shift: Saladworks and Frutta Bowls offer fully customizable, made-to-order salads and bowls; Garbanzo Mediterranean Fresh brings fresh, wholesome Mediterranean flavors to the category; and Barberitos rounds out the lineup with customizable fast-casual Mexican favorites. Franchise Growth Opportunities WOWorks is actively seeking experienced franchisees to join its better-for-you family of brands expanding portfolio. The platform has close to 240 restaurants operating nationwide, continues to lead the industry in innovation and growth opportunities for its franchisees, while ensuring that customers enjoy delicious and wholesome meals. For more information about franchise opportunities with WOWorks brands, visit woworksusa.com/a-place-to-invest/. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Mike’s Red Tacos, the celebrated San Diego-born beef Birria brand named as a Yelp Top 100 U.S. Restaurant (2023), has signed a 15-unit agreement with Michael Khalil to bring its signature drip to the Great Lakes State. The agreement, spearheaded by experienced restaurant owner and operator Michael Khalil, is expected to bring Mike’s Red Tacos’ signature birria and famous red tacos to Michigan over the next several years, with the first location planned for Royal Oak later this year. Khalil’s background combines both franchising and restaurant finance, beginning with a career in accounting before founding his own restaurant accounting firm. He later transitioned into franchise ownership and currently owns and operates 11 Little Caesars locations and 14 Jersey Mike’s restaurants across Michigan, Indiana and California. His extensive experience in restaurant operations, financial management and multi-unit franchising makes him a strong fit to lead Mike’s Red Tacos’ expansion into the Michigan market. “I’ve spent my career around restaurants and franchising, and I’ve always believed that the best concepts are built on exceptional food and strong leadership,” said Khalil. “Mike’s Red Tacos has both. From my first visit, I could see the care that goes into the product and the guest experience, and after getting to know the team behind the brand, I knew this was something I wanted to be a part of. I’m excited to help introduce Mike’s Red Tacos to Michigan and share a concept that I believe guests will really connect with.” The brand, first popularized in 2021 as a thriving food truck, carries a creative “the dip is worth the drip” tagline. It is best known for its craveable Birria, signature consomé dip and bold visual restaurant identity. As a result of two high-performing restaurants open within the past four years, Mike’s Red Tacos has attracted a social media following, especially with Millennial and Gen Z customers who value authenticity but also want a fun, approachable and shareable experience. “Michael brings a unique combination of restaurant expertise, financial acumen and hands-on operating experience that makes him an outstanding addition to the Mike’s Red Tacos family,” said Vincent Montanelli, President of Mike’s Red Tacos. “As we continue expanding across the country, we’re focused on partnering with operators who understand how to build strong teams, deliver a great guest experience and become a meaningful part of their communities. Michael has a proven track record of doing exactly that, and we’re excited to begin introducing Mike’s Red Tacos to Metro Detroit and, ultimately, communities throughout Michigan alongside him.” As Mike’s Red Tacos gears up to bring 15 new locations to Michigan, demand for the brand’s authentic birria and signature red tacos continues to soar. With more than 300 units already committed nationwide, territories are filling quickly, but opportunities to develop Mike’s Red Tacos remain available in major markets across the country for experienced operators eager to join one of the fastest-growing concepts in the industry. Built on quality, community, and a truly distinctive product, Mike’s Red Tacos has grown from a single food truck into a movement. Our founder, Mike, who has been hands-on since day one, has created a proven model that resonates with both guests and operators. The brand is now seeking experienced franchise owners and restaurant operators with strong business backgrounds and the ability to scale multiple locations, ensuring that more communities can experience Mike’s unmatched flavor, hospitality, and guest-focused culture. For more information about Mike’s Red Tacos, visit www.mikesredtacos.com. Connect with the brand’s pages for more details by visiting LinkedIn and Instagram. articles.title: QSR’s 20 Best Franchise Deals for 2026
articles.titleKo: QSR’s 20 Best Franchise Deals for 2026
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . For many years, franchising rewarded momentum. A compelling concept, solid unit growth, and a polished sales presentation were often enough to attract development interest. Not anymore. As inflation, higher labor costs, tighter lending standards, and shifting regulations reshaped the operating environment over the past year, prospective franchisees have become far more selective about where they invest. Excitement still matters, but it no longer closes the deal on its own. “The past year has really acted as a stress test, and not everyone passed,” says Liane Caruso, owner of helloCMO and cofounder of Franchise Assembly. “The brands that held up were the ones with lean, simple operations and realistic unit economics built for normal conditions.” That sentiment echoed across QSR’s 2026 Best Franchise Deals Council, a panel of franchise development, operations, marketing, legal, and investment experts assembled to help identify where the franchise industry is headed. The consensus was consistent. Franchise buyers are asking tougher questions than they were just a few years ago. They want proof instead of promises. They want to know how a concept performed when costs increased, labor tightened, and financing became more difficult—not simply how it grew during years of favorable market conditions. “A franchise that looks attractive on paper is selling a story. A strong franchise opportunity is selling proof,” says Michelle Rowan, president of Franchise Business Review. Today’s buyers, she says, are looking past projections to unit-level profitability, franchisee satisfaction, and candid validation from existing operators. Jonathan Hill, cofounder of Morrow Hill, has watched the same shift unfold from the real estate side. Inflation and labor pressures have forced brands to simplify operations, improve efficiency, and demonstrate predictable financial performance. “Clear, conservative financials and predictable cash flow are becoming table stakes,” he says. John Francis, whose franchise career spans more than three decades as a franchisee, franchisor, investor, and board member, believes prospective operators are also evaluating the strength of the organization behind the concept. “Paper looks the same for almost every brand,” he says. “What separates the real opportunities is operational discipline behind the curtain.” He argues the strongest systems have evolved beyond founder-led businesses into organizations with the infrastructure, leadership, and processes necessary to support long-term expansion. Those changing expectations explain why some brands continue signing development agreements while others struggle to fill their pipelines. Council members repeatedly pointed to the same characteristics. Winning franchise systems demonstrate durable unit economics instead of relying on exceptional performers. They simplify operations, embrace technology that improves productivity, offer flexible development options, and provide meaningful support long after opening day. These successful chains are also attracting experienced multi-unit operators who are evaluating whether the underlying business is built to scale. This year’s Best Franchise Deals list represents more than high-performing brands. They showcase franchise systems that have earned confidence through transparency, operational discipline, and a proven ability to help franchisees succeed in a more demanding business environment. articles.titleKo: The Rise of the Anti-Brand Bakery
articles.originalSummary: “Long live non-conformity,” says Cornish Bakery Founder Steve Grocutt as he debuts new RISE concept Fast growing Cornish Bakery is breaking the normal rules of expansion, turning its back on cookie-cutter brand building. The company has gone through three successful brand identities and is now starting afresh again. Founder Steve Grocutt says, “We’ve built a successful bakery brand with 81 locations and now we’re tearing it all apart. All on purpose. Five years ago, we took the DBA Gold award-winning Cornish Bakery brand we had honed at the time, and we completely ditched it! A lot of people thought we were mad, but I instinctively knew we had to move on. There was an urgency not to fall into a homogenous brand building category.” At the time, it was Grocutt’s mantra that led this direction. His simple, pioneering, guiding mantra: ‘bakery is the new coffee shop’ set the route. Five years on, Cornish Bakery’s growth has more than proven that statement to be spot on. The company has doubled its number of bakeries, grown the team to over 1,000, quadrupled profit and has developed enviable customer NPS scores of 75%. Steve continues, “We led with our vision to nourish people and reset the bakery design compass, all whilst delivering on our stated mission to redefine what a bakery is, does, and can be.” The team identified a handful of larger sites, spaces “crying out for that added extra” thus ‘RISE by Cornish Bakery’ was born, a bigger, bolder licensed brand extension. Sites in Betws-y-Coed, Wales, and Gunwharf Quays, Portsmouth, are now open and, in Grocutt’s words are, “already hammering it out of the park in every way possible.” “With RISE by Cornish Bakery we’ve reshaped what a bakery is does and can be. We’re thinning the boundary between bakeries/coffee shops and casual dining spaces, extending trading hours and integrating more deeply into the social fabric, the ‘vibe’, and the wishes and needs of the surrounding community – all led and driven by our brilliant colleagues on the ground.” The first RISE opened two months ago in Betws-y-Coed, Wales. The second is at Portsmouth’s historic Gunwharf Quays Designer Outlet where Cornish Bakery has relocated into a new two-storey, 3,500 sq. ft property as part of the centre’s redevelopment, making it the company’s largest site to date. RISE by Cornish Bakery Gunwharf Quays features an orangery, an outdoor terrace, a first-floor balcony, and dedicated space for community baking and barista classes. Alongside its signature pastries, cakes and coffee, RISE by Cornish Bakery introduces brunch and all-day small plates alongside Cornish beers from Harbour Brewery and still and sparkling wines from Camel Valley Vineyard. Grocutt states, “We’re taking the opposite of the cookie-cutter approach. We’re purposefully designing bespoke, flexible environments that showcase and optimise our bigger spaces, and experiential opportunities. These are already becoming places for the local community to host talks, exhibitions, classes and events But RISE by Cornish Bakery isn’t our end destination, it’s another exciting innovation on our much bigger journey of ongoing reinvention.” With the first couple of RISE by Cornish Bakery bakeries up and running, Grocutt is already far ahead, driving the next turn of the Cornish Bakery dial. articles.title: Cow & Sow to Open New Farm Shop & Kitchen in Autumn 2026
articles.titleKo: Cow & Sow to Open New Farm Shop & Kitchen in Autumn 2026
articles.originalSummary: Cow & Sow has announced The Field, a new farmshop and kitchen, will open opposite their Kitchen Farm, featuring a 70-seater restaurant/cafe and adjoining shop selling farm produce, fresh bread, butcher’s products and more Cow & Sow, the premium steakhouse brand with restaurants in Bristol and Birmingham has announced the opening of The Field Farmshop & Kitchen, which is set to open in Autumn 2026. Once known as the Dew Drop Inn and more recently The Jubilee, the site has been shuttered for more than three years and will undergo a change of use transformation, led by founder Mark Warbuton and his wife Amy. Sitting within almost an acre of land, the property is located opposite Cow & Sow’s recently launched Kitchen Farm in Flax Bourton, just outside of Bristol. The Field farm shop will sell home-grown produce delivered daily from the farm, as well as fresh bread, dairy products, pantry staples and butchery, in partnership with Cow & Sow’s British meat suppliers. The shop will also feature a florist, plus a gift and homewares section. Open from morning until 6pm, The Field will also be home to a 70-seater restaurant/cafe, serving up a range of hearty breakfast, brunch and lunch offerings including fresh salads, quiches, soups and ploughman’s platters, all freshly prepared onsite. Guests will also be able to enjoy coffee, using beans from Clifton Coffee Roasters, plus refreshing drinks from a bar. Behind the building, external decking will give a further 40-plus guests the opportunity to dine al fresco, or enjoy a drink from the bar, whilst taking in the stunning countryside views. The Field will stay open into the evening on selected days, giving locals and visitors the chance to catch up and enjoy the last rays of sunshine. Cow & Sow has also revealed ambitious plans for a phase two of the development, creating meeting and event spaces available to hire, plus a test kitchen and cookery school on the first floor of the building. Offering masterclasses and courses both in the test kitchens and over fire on the terrace, Cow & Sow and the team at The Field will be collaborating with experts including Roam Catering’s Ross Anderson, an expert in fireside cooking and judge for the World Steak Challenge competition and Ben Naylor from Somerset Grill Co, who are both currently working with the Cow & Sow team. Mark Warburton, founder of Cow & Sow, said: “It’s been a really exciting start to the year for us, we’ve already introduced our Kitchen Farm and now Amy and I are bringing The Field Farmshop & Kitchen into the wider family. We’re passionate about using and growing the very best produce in our restaurants and sourcing it from as locally as possible, and we want to share that passion with the people of Bristol and beyond. “I really want this space to become a place to gather, enjoy and celebrate for locals and visitors and we’re already working with our friends at Clifton Coffee Roasters, Walter Rose & Son, Roam Catering and Somerset Grill Co to make sure we’re able to offer something really special. We can’t wait to welcome people through the doors this autumn.” To be the first to get updates on The Field, follow the journey on Instagram at: https://www.instagram.com/thefieldfarmshop/
